A creature’s Health also affects the depth of its 
health pool. Its Health is multiplied by the number of 
Health Dice it possesses, and the result is added to its 
health pool. For example, if a creature has a Health of 
+1 and 2d8 Health Dice, its health pool has a depth of 
2d8 + 2 (average 11).

speed.content:
A monster’s speed tells you how far it can move on its 
turn. For more information on speed, see the “Playing 
the Game” chapter.
All creatures have an overland speed, simply called 
the creature’s speed. Creatures that have no form of 
ground-based locomotion have an overland speed of 
0 feet.
Some creatures have one or more of the following 
additional movement modes.

burrow.content:
A creature that has a burrowing speed can use that 
speed to move through sand, earth, mud, or ice. A 
creature can’t burrow through solid rock unless it has a 
special trait that allows it to do so.

climb.content:
A creature that has a climbing speed can use all or 
part of its movement to move on vertical surfaces. 
The creature doesn’t need to spend extra movement 
to climb.

fly.content:
A creature that has a flying speed can use all or part of 
its movement to fly. Some creatures have the ability to 
hover, which makes them hard to knock out of the air. 
Such a creature stops hovering when it dies.

swim.content:
A creature that has a swimming speed doesn’t need to 
spend extra movement to swim.

abilities.content:
Every creature has six abilities (Strength, Agility, 
Health, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Presence). For 
more information on abilities and how they’re used in 
play, see the “Playing the Game” chapter.

saving_checks.content:
The saving checks entry is reserved for creatures that 
are adept at resisting certain kinds of effects. For 
example, a creature that isn’t easily enraptured or 
frightened might list a Wisdom saving check. Most 
creatures don’t have special saving checks, in which 
case this section is absent.
A saving check bonus is the sum of a creature’s 
relevant ability and its proficiency bonus, which is 
determined by the creature’s challenge score (as shown 
in the Proficiency Bonus by Challenge Score table).

skill_scores.content:
The skill scores entry is reserved for creatures that 
are proficient in one or more skills. Unlike characters 
who have skill bonuses, nonplayer creatures have skill 
scores. For example, a creature that is very perceptive 
and stealthy might have listed skill scores in Wisdom 
(Perception) and Agility (Stealth) checks.
A skill score is equal to 10 + a creature’s relevant 
ability and its proficiency bonus, which is determined 
by the creature’s challenge score (as shown in the 
Proficiency Bonus by Challenge Score table). Other 
bonuses or penalties might apply. For instance, a 
creature might have a larger-than-expected bonus 
(usually double its proficiency bonus) to account for 
its heightened expertise.

Vulnerabilities, Resistances, 
and Immunities
Some creatures have vulnerability, resistance, or 
immunity to certain types of damage. Particular 
creatures are even resistant or immune to damage 
from nonmagical attacks (a magical attack is an attack 
delivered by a spell, a magic item, or another magical 
source). In addition, some creatures are immune to 
certain conditions.

senses.content:
The senses entry notes a creature’s primary sense or 
senses:

feeling.content:
A feeling creature primarily uses its sense of touch and 
vibrations to feel its way through the world. Usually, 
a feeling creature cannot detect unmoving objects 
farther than 5 feet away.
Tremorsense. A creature with tremorsense can 
detect and pinpoint the origin of vibrations within 
a specific radius, provided that the creature and the

hearing.content:
A hearing creature primarily uses its hearing to sense 
creatures and moving objects. Usually, a hearing 
creature cannot detect silent, unmoving objects.
Echolocation. A few creatures, like bats, use 
echolocation, a type of advanced hearing that relies 
on echoes to sense even stationary objects and silent 
creatures.

sighted.content:
A sighted creature primarily uses its vision to sense 
creatures and objects in dim or bright light.
Darkvision. A creature with darkvision can see in 
the dark within a specific radius. The creature can 
see in dim light within the radius as if it were bright 
light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. The 
creature can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of 
gray. Many creatures that live underground have this 
special sense.

smelling.content:
A smelling creature primarily uses its sense of smell to 
detect creatures and identify objects. Some smelling 
creatures, like a mastiff, can detect scent trails that are 
otherwise undetectable.

sixth_sense.content:
A creature with a sixth sense can, out to a specific 
range, perceive in normal and magical darkness, detect 
scent trails and all sounds, experience flavor and 
touch from afar, sense invisible creatures and objects, 
automatically detect visual illusions and succeed 
on saving checks against them, and perceive the 
original form of a shapechanger or a creature that is 
transformed by magic. Furthermore, the creature can 
perceive the Ethereal Plane within the same range.

languages.content:
The languages that a creature can articulate are listed 
in alphabetical order. Sometimes a monster can 
understand a language but can’t articulate it, and this 
is noted in its entry. A “—” indicates that a creature 
neither articulates nor understands any language.

telepathy.content:
Telepathy is a magical ability that allows a creature to 
communicate mentally with another creature within 
a specified range. The contacted creature doesn’t need 
to share a language with the creature to communicate 
in this way with it, but it must be able to understand 
at least one language. A creature without telepathy can 
receive and respond to telepathic messages but can’t 
initiate or terminate a telepathic conversation.
A telepathic creature doesn’t need to perceive a 
contacted creature and can end the telepathic contact 
at any time. The contact is broken as soon as the two 
creatures are no longer within range of each other or 
if the telepathic creature contacts a different creature 
within range. A telepathic creature can initiate or 
terminate a telepathic conversation without using 
an action, but if the creature is incapacitated, it can’t 
initiate telepathic contact, and any current contact is 
terminated.
A creature within the area of an antimagic field or in 
any other location where magic doesn’t function can’t 
send or receive telepathic messages.

challenge.content:
A creature’s challenge score tells you how great a 
threat the creature is. An appropriately equipped and 
well-rested party of four characters should be able to 
defeat a creature that has a challenge score equal to its 
steps taken without suffering any deaths. For example, 
a party of four 3rd-step characters should find a 
creature with a challenge score of 3 to be a worthy 
challenge, but not a deadly one.
Creatures that are significantly weaker than 1st-
step characters have a challenge score lower than 1. 
Creatures with a challenge score of 0 are insignificant 
except in large numbers; those with no effective 
attacks are worth no

experience_points.content:
The number of experience points (XP) a monster 
is worth is based on its challenge score. Experience 
points are awarded for defeating the creature or by 
neutralizing the threat posed by the creature through 
trickery, diplomacy, or nonviolent contest.
Unless something tells you otherwise, a creature 
summoned by a spell or other magical ability is worth 
the XP noted in its stat block.

special_traits.content:
Special traits (which appear after a creature’s 
challenge score but before any actions or reactions) 
are characteristics that are likely to be relevant in a 
combat encounter and that require some explanation.

innate_spellcasting.content:
A creature with the innate ability to cast spells has 
the Innate

spellcasting.content:
A creature with the Spellcasting special trait has a step 
number and spell slots, which it uses to cast its spells 
of 1st level and higher. The spellcaster's step number is 
also used for any cantrips included in the feature.
A creature can cast a spell from its list at a higher 
level if it has the spell slot to do so. For example, a 
s
When a creature takes its action, it can choose from 
the options in the Actions section of its stat block or 
use one of the actions available to all creatures, such as 
the Dash or Hide action, as described in the “Running 
the Game” chapter.
Reach and Ranged Attacks
Two actions that a creature can take in combat are 
reach and ranged attacks. These can be spell attacks 
or weapon attacks, where the “weapon” might be a 
manufactured item or a natural weapon, such as a 
claw or tail spike. For more information on different 
kinds of attacks, see the “Playing the Game” chapter.
Creature vs. Target. The target of a reach or ranged 
attack is usually either one creature or one target, the 
difference being that a “target” can be a creature or an 
object.
Hit. Any damage inflicted or other effects that occur 
as a result of an attack hitting a target are described 
after the “Hit” notation. You have the option of 
inflicting average damage or rolling the damage; for 
this reason, both the average damage and the die 
expression are presented.
Miss. If an attack has an effect that occurs on a 
miss, that information is presented after the “Miss” 
notation.
Multiattack
A creature that can make multiple attacks on its 
turn has the Multiattack action. A creature can’t use 
Multiattack when making an opportunity attack, 
which must be a single reach attack.

Special Traits
Special traits (which appear after a creature’s 
challenge score but before any actions or reactions) 
are characteristics that are likely to be relevant in a 
combat encounter and that require some explanation.
Innate Spellcasting
A creature with the innate ability to cast spells has 
the Innate Spellcasting special trait. Unless noted 
otherwise, an innate spell of 1st level or higher is 
always cast at its lowest possible level and can’t be cast 
at a higher level. If a creature has a cantrip where its 
level matters and no level is given, use the creature’s 
challenge score.
An innate spell can have special rules or restrictions. 
For example, a creature might be able to innately 
cast the levitate spell, but the spell has a “self only” 
restriction, which means that the spell affects only the 
spellcaster.
A creature’s innate spells can’t be swapped out with 
other spells. If a creature’s innate spells don’t require 
attack rolls, no attack bonus is given for them.
Spellcasting
A creature with the Spellcasting special trait has a step 
number and spell slots, which it uses to cast its spells 
of 1st level and higher. The spellcaster's step number is 
also used for any cantrips included in the feature.

level if it has the spell slot to do so. For example, a

When a creature takes its action, it can choose from 
the options in the Actions section of its stat block or 
use one of the actions available to all creatures, such as 
the Dash or Hide action, as described in the “Running 
the Game” chapter.

reach_and_ranged_attacks.content:
Two actions that a creature can take in combat are 
reach and ranged attacks. These can be spell attacks 
or weapon attacks, where the “weapon” might be a 
manufactured item or a natural weapon, such as a 
claw or tail spike. For more information on different 
kinds of attacks, see the “Playing the Game” chapter.
Creature vs. Target. The target of a reach or ranged 
attack is usually either one creature or one target, the 
difference being that a “target” can be a creature or an 
object.
Hit. Any damage inflicted or other effects that occur 
as a result of an attack hitting a target are described 
after the “Hit” notation. You have the option of 
inflicting average damage or rolling the damage; for 
this reason, both the average damage and the die 
expression are presented.
Miss. If an attack has an effect that occurs on a 
miss, that information is presented after the “Miss” 
notation.

multiattack.content:
A creature that can make multiple attacks on its 
turn has the Multiattack action. A creature can’t use 
Multiattack when making an opportunity attack, 
which must be a single reach attack.

ammunition.content:
A creature carries enough ammunition to make its 
ranged attacks. You can assume that a creature has 
2d4 pieces of ammunition for a thrown weapon 
attack, and 2d10 pieces of ammunition for a projectile 
weapon such as a bow or crossbow.

reactions.content:
If a creature can do something special with its 
reaction, that information is contained here. If a 
creature has no special reaction, this section is absent.

limited_usage.content:
Some special abilities have restrictions on the number 
of times they can be used.
X/Day. The notation “X/Day” means a special 
ability can be used X number of times and that a 
creature must finish a long rest to regain expended 
uses. For example, “1/Day” means a special ability can 
be used once and that the creature must finish a long 
rest to use it again.
Recharge X–Y. The notation “Recharge X–Y” means 
that a creature can use a special ability once and that 
the ability then has a random chance of recharging 
during each subsequent round of combat. At the 
start of each of the creature’s turns, roll a d6. If the 
roll is one of the numbers in the recharge notation, 
the creature regains the use of the special ability. The 
ability also recharges when the creature finishes a short 
or long rest.
For example, “Recharge 5–6” means a creature can 
use the special ability once. Then, at the start of the 
creature’s turn, it regains the use of that ability if it 
rolls a 5 or 6 on a d6.
Recharge after a Short or Long Rest. This 
notation means that a creature can use a special ability 
once and then must finish a short or long rest to use it 
again.

aboleth.content:
Aboleths are massive eldritch sea serpents. Scholars 
speculate that they originated from a sea between 
worlds, but now dwell in Material Planes in their 
deepest waters. Having lived before the rise and fall of 
ancient civilizations, most aboleths are millennia—if 
not eons—old. They have inherent psychic power that 
they used to communicate with each other during 
the height of their own culture. However, once in 
contact with people, aboleths realized their psychic 
abilities often overwhelmed and easily enraptured 
mortal minds.
Some aboleths have chosen to use this power for 
their own gain, enrapturing people to accomplish 
tasks and build their own power. However, other 
aboleths have learned to restrain their abilities to 
avoid overwhelming people, and instead use it to assist 
them. Certain aboleths use their knowledge of mortal 
desires to help struggling communities or travelers, 
or provide refuge—sometimes in the water itself, 
using the odd properties of their own mucus—to 
those seeking to escape danger or unsafe situations. 
While uncommon, there are those who say they were 
raised by an aboleth, who rescued them after fleeing a 
hazardous home.
Seizing Rules for Monsters
Many creatures have special attacks that allow them to quickly 
seize prey. When a creature hits with such an attack, it doesn’t 
need to make an additional ability check to determine whether 
the seizing succeeds, unless the attack says otherwise.
A character seized by the creature can use their action to try 
to escape. To do so, they must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) 
or Agility (Acrobatics) check against the escape DS in the 
creature’s stat block. If no escape DS is given, assume the DS is 
the creature’s Strength (Athletics) skill score. 
A

alchemical_familiar.content:
Alchemical familiars are small constructs synthesized 
from inorganic material, rare herbs, and reagents. 
These crafted familiars are bound to their creator by 
a drop of the alchemist’s blood, which awakens the 
familiar from its inert state. Through their bond, an 
alchemical familiar and its creator share knowledge 
and perception so long as they remain on the 
same plane. The herbs used to create an alchemical 
familiar infuse its otherwise insignificant bite with an 
incapacitating toxin. Such familiars are often used as 
assistants, messengers, or spies.

angels.content:
Often depicted as exquisite humanoids with luminous 
wings, angels are celestial creatures that act as the 
hands and feet of deities. Created by gods, these 
legendary celestials enact the will of the deity they 
serve, whether as messengers, soldiers, or arbiters. 
While they are traditional natives to higher planes, 
they can be found in whatever realm a god has made 
their domain. 
Most angels are moral champions, made by 
deities who embody respectable ideals, for wicked 
and malevolent gods prefer more fiendish servitors. 
However, angels are not beholden to goodness, and 
those that choose another path are often considered 
“fallen” by others. Those that embrace evil pursuits 
often reflect it in their appearance, such as with dark 
wings. 
In addition, while angels are typically seen in a 
humanoid appearance, they are rumored to have 
another form that is far more incognizable to mortal 
perceptions. As to not disturb mortal sensibilities, they 
often prefer a more humanoid appearance for such 
affairs unless their duty involves striking such terror.
Cherubs
With two pairs of wings, cherubs occupy the middle 
of the hierarchy of angels. These celestials are often 
tasked by their gods with assignments in other planes 
that are too dangerous for a deva to complete or hold 
the rank of captains in celestial armies.

animated_objects.content:
Oftentimes, powerful spellcasters such as archmages 
or mighty sorcerers enchant mundane objects with 
incredible arcane power to animate them. These 
animated objects are most often used as guardians 
to protect the spellcaster’s domain or secrets, but a 
creative individual could find other uses for them 
as well.
While not typical, some spellcasters are so strong 
that they can imbue animated objects with sentience. 
Other times, an animated object naturally develops 
sentience if it has been animated by magic for decades 
or longer.
Animated Armor
For a reclusive archmage deep in study, armored 
guards need not only lodging, but pay, and can be 
quite the distraction. Hence, animating a suit of 
armor is a simple way to have loyal guards that need 
very little maintenance and do not interrupt any work. 
Relentless defenders, animated armors protect what 
they have been assigned to with unyielding dedication 
until they are too damaged to move or until the 
enchantment that animates them is unraveled.

ankhegs.content:
These enormous insectoid monsters are natively found 
throughout the Material Planes in nearly every biome 
aside from the most inhospitable. Scholars note that 
ankheg colonies seem to act as a unified entity, with 
their societies drawing parallels to people’s civilizations 
in the way they divide labor, communicate with each 
other, and solve complex problems.
While ankhegs are not necessarily aggressive if left 
alone, their colonies can often grow near people’s 
settlements, where they can exploit nearby resources 
for the sake of expanding and developing their 
homes, and defend themselves if they feel threatened. 
Oftentimes, this can lead to conflict with nearby 
towns and cities. 
A

apes.content:
These tailless primates are native to forests, especially 
rainforests, and include specific beasts such as 
orangutans, gorillas, and chimpanzees. They are 
omnivores, but lean mostly toward eating plants. 
Exposure to magic and other environmental factors 
can contribute to a subspecies of giant apes. While 
fairly territorial, careful travelers can avoid hostility 
if they are careful and respectful while within a giant 
ape’s territory.

archmage.content:
Archmages are powerful (and usually quite old) 
spellcasters dedicated to the study of the arcane arts. 
Benevolent ones counsel kings and queens, while 
evil ones rule as tyrants and pursue lichdom. Those 
who are neither good nor evil sequester themselves 
in remote towers to practice their magic without 
interruption. An archmage typically has one or more 
apprentice mages, and an archmage’s abode has 
numerous magical wards and guardians to discourage 
interlopers.

azer.content:
Made of semi-fluid magma, azers are elemental beings 
native to igneous lands. While their fiery forms make 
it difficult for them to safely interact with people, 
they enjoy learning about other cultures. Azer society 
has a deep regard and appreciation for artistry and 
craftsmanship, and they contribute to it in forms that 
require heat, such as glass-blowing and blacksmithing.
They can reflexively harden sections of their bodies, 
which acts as a sort of natural armor, but rather than 
rely entirely on their natural fire for weapons, azers 
like to show off their craftsmanship with handmade 
hammers and shields.

bandits.content:
When desperate times lead to desperation, some 
people turn to banditry to make their living in an 
unrelenting world. By pilfering from others, bandits 
thrive—or just manage to survive.
While some bandits are driven by survival, others 
are driven by greed, and still others act as rebels. Some 
bandits stand against tyranny, stealing only from those 
who would oppress others, sharing their loot with 
those in need.
Most bands of bandits are led by a captain, a leader 
who commands the others through either 
intimidation or charisma.

Defense Score 12 (leather armor)
Health Pool 11 (2d8 + 2), or 9 (2d6 + 2) if Small

basilisk.content:
Known as the “sovereigns of serpents,” basilisks are 
subterranean monsters best described as sizable, 
sinuous reptiles having anywhere from three to five 
sets of legs. Their tough scales have a muted but 
variable coloration depending on their environment; 
a more humid underground produces cool colors 
like blue or green, while drier surroundings make for 
warmer colors, such as red or orange. An environment 
steeped in magic can lead to more vibrant or unusual 
scale colors.
Basilisks have a poisonous bite, but are most 
infamous for their petrifying gaze. Anyone who can 
see into its eyes is seized by stone, unless their will is 
stronger than the basilisk’s. Otherwise, the victim is 
doomed to be a statue lost in a basilisk’s underground 
territory.

other magic.
A sighted creature that isn’t surprised can avert its

does so, it can’t see the basilisk until the start of its next 
turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If it looks at the 
basilisk in the meantime, it must immediately make the 
check. This trait has no effect on a blind creature.
If the basilisk sees its reflection within 30 feet of it in 
bright light, it mistakes itself for a rival and targets itself 
with its gaze.

bats.content:
Small mammals with winged forelimbs, bats are 
nocturnal creatures that use echolocation to perceive 
the world around them. They are found in many 
different environments, such as woodlands, deserts, 
caves, and even towns. Depending on the subspecies, 
bats eat insects, fruit, or nectar. However, some bats 
feed on blood, and thus have associated the species 
as a whole with vampires. While giant bats are not as 
dangerous as they look, they are often hunted out of 
fear that they could be a vampire.
B

bears.content:
Bears are sizable mammals, typically solitary, that 
hibernate during the winter. Black bears are generally 
creatures of forests and open alpine habitats, while 
brown bears are less restricted in their habitats, being 
found in deserts, mountain forests, tundras, alpine 
meadows, and along coasts. While black and brown 
bears are omnivores, polar bears are carnivorous and 
are found in arctic regions.

behir.content:
As evolutionary cousins to dragons, fully grown behirs 
would resemble something between young and adult 
dragons, if it weren’t for their ten legs. When their 
forebears were left in underground caverns, behirs’ 
growth was restricted by the size of their subterranean 
tunnels. While behirs cannot fly and most no longer 
have the appendages to allow such movement, some 
still retain vestigial wings. Their scale colors are usually 
white or grey, but sometimes can be mottled with 
other hues which, much like dragons, are dependent 
on what region their cavernous homes are within.
Most behirs breathe lightning, though other 
elemental variations have been rumored. Behirs hoard 
anything they personally consider valuable—this could 
be anything from treasure in the form of gold and 
riches, to power through magical items and artifacts, 
to knowledge in rare tomes and ancient scrolls.

22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage.
Constrict. DS 16 Weapon Attack: reach 5 ft., one Large or 
smaller creature. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage 
plus 17 (2d10 + 6) slashing damage. The target is seized 
(escape DS 16) if the behir isn’t already constricting 
a creature, and the target is restrained until this

Lightning Breath (Recharge 5–6). The behir exhales a 
line of lightning that is 20 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each 
creature in that line must make a DS 16 Agility saving

check, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Swallow. The behir makes one bite attack against a 
Medium or smaller target it is seizing. If the attack

ends. While swallowed, the target is disoriented and 
restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other 
effects outside the behir, and it suffers 21 (6d6) acid 
damage at the start of each of the behir’s turns. A behir 
can have only one creature swallowed at a time.
If the behir suffers 30 damage or more on a single

succeed on a DS 14 Health saving check at the end of 
that turn or regurgitate the creature, which falls prone 
in a space within 10 feet of the behir. If the behir dies, a 
swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can 
escape from the corpse by using 15 feet of movement, 
exiting prone.

berserker.content:
Hailing from hinterlands, berserkers come together 
in war parties for eliminating threats or conquering 
enemies.
B

blood_hawk.content:
Taking its name from its crimson feathers and 
aggressive nature, the blood hawk fearlessly attacks 
almost any animal, stabbing it with its daggerlike 
beak. Blood hawks flock together in large numbers, 
attacking as a pack to take down prey.

boars.content:
These wild swine with bristly hides are social animals 
of importance to many people. Boars are often 
domesticated to be used as a food source but are 
also a common game animal for hunting. They are 
omnivores with varied habitats that include jungles, 
grasslands, and forests with dense vegetation. Giant 
boars can cause immense damage to crops and small 
villages if incited into aggression, but are a prized 
hunting trophy if they can be taken down.

bulette.content:
Colloquially known as landsharks, bulettes are 
earth-devouring monsters that lurk in uninhabited 
regions of the world. With powerful jaws and hulking 
muscles, bulettes carve through earth and rock with 
unnerving ease. They have a purely carnivorous diet 
supplemented by minerals in the earth, and their 
strong muscles allow them to leap incredible distances 
to catch their prey.
A bulette’s thick hide is difficult to penetrate; 
the creature has very few natural predators and is a 
dangerous force to be dealt with if travelers or settlers 
enter its territory. Their coloration depends highly on 
the environment where they were born, as their hide 
takes on a hue that helps them blend in with their 
surroundings when above ground.

These hooved animals native to deserts are distinctive 
because of the one or two “humps” on their backs. 
Often domesti

cat.content:
These small, domesticated, carnivorous felines are 
prolific throughout most Material Planes. While some 
are feral, living on their own in either the wilds or 
on city streets, others are kept as pets by leaders and 
common folk alike. The natural dexterity, elegant 
grace, and keen senses of cats make them popular 
among spellcasters as familiars.
B

centaurs.content:
Most centaurs assume they are the bastard children 
of some nature god. Many believe they are the 
creation of an elven nature spirit that bore them from 
the ground to protect nature. But because of the 
uncertainty of their origins they don’t worship any god 
or spirit for fear of angering the one that made them.
The People
Centaurs seem half person, half horse. Their person 
half can look as varied as any other people. 
They form semi-nomadic groups that travel in large 
herds across grasslands. The herd size fluctuates, as 
different clans may join or leave at any given moment. 
They stand as defenders of the land, nurturing injured 
creatures and fending off people who would destroy 
their natural habitat. They have excellent relations 
with people of any ancestry who are dedicated to 
preserving the land. They can be fierce allies or 
hated foes.
Centaur Template
This template can be applied to any person stat 
block. The person keeps their statistics, except as 
noted below.
Challenge. The centaur’s challenge score usually 
increases by 1. To be certain, recalculate the score after 
you apply the template.
Type. The centaur’s creature type is fey, rather than 
person.
Size. The centaur’s size is Large, and their Health 
Dice are d10s.
Speed. The centaur’s speed is 50 feet.
Charge. If the centaur moves at least 30 feet 
straight toward a target and then hits it with a reach 
attack on the same turn, the target suffers an extra 10 
(3d6) damage of the same type.
New Action: Hooves. The centaur can attack with 
their hooves, inflicting bludgeoning damage equal to 
2d6 + their Strength on a hit.

chimera.content:
There are many legends about how these mythical 
monsters—composed of the parts of several beasts—
came to be. Some say they are the product of wizard 
experimentation, others speculate that they emerged 
once the land healed from a great war where dragon 
blood was spilled, and still more claim they are the 
creations of young, fumbling gods.
A chimera is depicted in tavern tales as a monster 
with a lion’s head and body, a dragon’s head and 
wings, a goat’s head, and a serpent for a tail. Other 
variations are rumored to exist, though all of them 
C

chuul.content:
The sea between worlds is a vast, fathomless 
expanse only barely known by people. Where its 
boundaries blur, creating a “shore,” chuul emerge 
onto physical realms. Crustacean-like creatures with 
thick exoskeletons, chuuls have tentacles that carry a 
numbing toxin and enormous pincers that can easily 
restrain even a large beast.
For reasons unknown to observing scholars, 
chuuls are drawn to magic—whether that be ancient 
sites with storied histories, great spellcasters of 
unfathomable power, or incredible artifacts hidden 
deep from mortal eyes. Chuuls guard these sources of 
magic and, in their own unusual way, seem to silently 
observe and study them.

cloaker.content:
These flat-bodied creatures were once inhabitants of 
the sea between worlds. While in motion, cloakers 
resemble boneless ocean rays, but while resting 
with their underside against a surface they are near 
indistinguishable from leather cloaks—hence their 
colloquial name. They are cunning predators that can 
attach themselves to prey and suffocate them.
Cloakers lurk underground in dark caverns and 
catacombs and know their territory well. They are 
guileful, gaining the upper hand or tactically fleeing 
by summoning illusions of themselves, and respect 
wily thinking. Cloakers are capable of speech, but 
don’t communicate above a whisper; anything louder 
is a moan that fills people with unnatural terror. 
C

cockatrice.content:
A cockatrice is a small monster resembling a dragon’s 
serpentine form on two chicken legs with a rooster’s 
head and draconic wings. The bite of its beak induces 
petrification—not its gaze, as with a basilisk, though 
the two are frequently confused by the average person. 
In areas where they are common, cockatrices are pests; 
to keep them at bay, people train weasels, who are 
strangely immune to a cockatrice’s petrification.

commoner.content:
Commoners include peasants, serfs, servants, pilgrims, 
merchants, artisans, and hermits.
C

concubus.content:
Concubi are fiends that feast on an energy created by 
people while they intensely experience an emotion, 
such as anger, fear, or joy. Love—romantic, platonic, 
or familial—is said to provide the most worthwhile 
food for a concubus. In their natural form, a concubus 
is a beautiful humanoid with horns, bat-like wings, 
hooves, and a pointed tail. However, they can take the 
form of another person with ease.
Some concubi use their shapechanging and 
enthralling powers to gather their food by force, but 
others have learned that naturally occurring emotions 
of accomplishment, self-love, and understanding 
are much more nourishing. A concubus might 
reside in a small town as an innkeeper, their true 
nature unknown as they help solve relationship 
issues between lovers and friends in order to sustain 
themselves and preserve the happiness of the people 
around them.

polymorph into a Small or Medium person, or back into 
its true form. Without wings, the concubus loses its 
flying speed. Other than its size and speed, its statistics 
are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing 
or carrying isn’t transformed. It reverts to its true form if 
it dies.
Telepathic Bond. The concubus ignores the range 
restriction on its telepathy when communicating with a 
creature it has enraptured. The two don’t even need to 
be on the same plane of existence.
Actions

ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.

or be magically enraptured for 1 day. At the end of 
each day that a concubus doesn’t successfully charm a 
target in this way, it automatically suffers one level of 
exhaustion. A willing target can choose to automatically 
fail the saving check. The enraptured creature regards 
the concubus as a trusted friend to be heeded and 
protected. Although the target isn’t under the concubus’s 
control, it takes the concubus’s requests or actions in the 
most favorable way it can. If the target suffers any harm, 
it can repeat the saving check, ending the effect on a 
success. The effect immediately ends if the concubus 
suggests a course of action that would harm the target. If 
the target successfully saves against the effect, or if the 
effect on it ends, the target is immune to this concubus’s 
Charm for the next 24 hours.
The concubus can have only one target enraptured at a 
time. If it enraptures another, the effect on the previous 
target ends.
Kiss. The concubus kisses a willing creature. For the next 
24 hours, the concubus and the target each gain a +2 
bonus to defense and resistance to psychic damage, and 
the target cannot be enraptured by any other creature

couatl.content:
These radiant, feathered serpents are crafted by 
gods to act as stewards and collectors of lore and 
knowledge. Couatl are sent by their deities to walk 
and live amongst people, learn their stories and 
history, and record that knowledge for preservation 
in celestial archives. To achieve this, couatl have 
the ability to change their shape and are afforded 
protections for their minds so that sinister powers 
don’t uncover them.
Often while in pursuit of their goal, couatls 
become invested in and protective of the people 
they have been tasked to mingle with. While couatls 
are dedicated to their scholarly duties, they can 
accomplish those while remaining close to the people 
they are fond of, becoming advisors, defenders, or 
even just traveling companions.

Actions

In a new form, the couatl retains its game statistics

crabs.content:
Crabs are crustaceans with a flat body surrounded 
by a chitinous exoskeleton. They are omnivorous, 
consuming a balance of plant and animal matter, and 
are found in both saltwater and freshwater habitats. 
When provoked, crabs often act aggressively, especially 
toward each other. This behavior creates a problem 
when applied to the giant subspecies of crab, who can 
easily make rocky caverns and shores dangerous places 
to tread and explore.

gather in tropical, freshwater habitats. They are swift 
swimmers and have powerful jaws, which make them 
dangerous predators. Crocodiles are sensitive to the

darkmantle.content:
These small monsters are riddled throughout many 
material planes’ underground caverns. Predatory 
creatures, darkmantles have an exterior skin that 
looks not unlike stone, allowing them to curl within 
themselves and take on the appearance of a rock 
formation. They hunt best when able to ambush from 
above, giving them an easy way to enfold and suffocate 
their prey. 
If they are in a disadvantageous situation, 
darkmantles can conjure magical darkness to get the 
upper hand. It is also their primary defense against 
their main predator, the cloakers, which find hunting 
darkmantles to be a unique challenge.
C

deer.content:
Deers are hoofed, herbivorous mammals that live 
in a variety of biomes—commonly in forests and 
grasslands, but they can also be found in tundras and 
rainforests. In most species, males grow impressive 
antlers, while the females don’t. In regions where they 
are plentiful, deer are commonly hunted for their 
meat and hide.

demons.content:
There are a multitude of fates for a person’s soul at 
the time of their death. For those of particular infamy 
and evil, one of those fates is being cast into the 
lower planes and into the hands of fiends. Of the two 
kinds of fiends that hold dominion over the nether 
realms, demons are jailers, overseers, and soldiers—
ensuring that the souls they hold remain to receive the 
punishment they deserve by preventing escape and 
stopping incursions from would-be rescuers.
Should a strong soul declare intent to improve 
themselves from their mortal nature, they may have 
the opportunity to become an intelligent demon if 
they are judged to have bettered themselves.
However, after a lifetime spent in eternal service 
watching over the worst of people, there are plenty of 
demons who are dissatisfied with their charge. Some 
are motivated to find their own way, but others seek to 
destroy the worlds that would produce such despicable 
souls. 
Balor
The mightiest of demons, balors are enormous 
horned giants with massive bat-like wings. They are 
infused with sulphurous power, which grants them 
preternatural might, but is unleashed in an inferno 
upon their demise. Balors are typically generals of 
demon armies, the wardens over entire cell blocks of 
souls, or the guards for the very worst souls the depths 
contain. Those very same souls are usually the ones 
with the will to become balors themselves, but such 
souls have the greatest hurdle to overcome: pride.
D

In the lowest planes are the fortress prisons where 
fiends intern the souls of villainous people that are 
cast into their depths. Devils are the bureaucratic 
backbone of these oubliettes, acting as arbiters, 
tormenters, and administrators. They determine the

devotee.content:
A devotee zealously walks the path of an uncommon 
religion. An evil devotee might worship a demon 
lord, archdevil, or eldritch abomination, while a more 
benevolent devotee might simply worship a dead 
god, obscure demigod, otherworldly entity, or even a 
fallen mortal they hope to deify. Some devotees pledge 
themselves to a cause, lifestyle, or philosophy instead 
of an entity of veneration.
Some devotees organize themselves into a group, led 
by a charismatic champion of their cause or religion. 
Others live and die by a faith that they might have in 
common with no one else.

dinosaurs.content:
Diverse and magnificent reptiles, dinosaurs are 
primordial beasts that roamed the planes since they 
were still new. They dwelt within the seas, dominated 
the lands, and mastered the skies, and were as likely to 
be apex predators as they were to be migratory grazers. 
Many cultures reference dinosaurs in myths and 
legends, and ancient craftsmanship often depicts their 
mighty forms in varied interpretations.
It is commonly considered that dinosaurs were 
victims of historical calamities that shaped the 
multiverse. However, in the wildest reaches of the 
world it is rumored that some of them yet survive, 
sovereigns of a land that is untouched by the ravages 
of time. 
Plesiosaurus
The plesiosaurus is a carnivorous predator that dwells 
in marine habitats. They are agile swimmers propelled 
by two sets of fins on a turtle-shaped torso, and have 
a neck nearly the length of their body. Plesiosaurus 
are smaller than many of their terrestrial cousins and 
also differ by giving live birth rather than their young 
hatching from eggs. Due to water routes, some claim 
to have seen plesiosaurus in waters closer to people’s 
lands—though some even swear they have seen them 
in entirely closed lakes.

dogs.content:
Domesticated from wild wolves, dogs are carnivorous 
canines that throughout history have been reliable 
companions for people of all lands. Bred throughout 
the ages into many different subspecies, dogs come 
in incredibly diverse shapes, sizes, and colorations. 
Depending on their owner, they can be hunters, 
helpers, laborers, defenders, or simply companions. 
A well-treated dog is loyal to its owner and comes to 
their aid for almost anything. Given the prominence 
of dogs and their notable attributes, it is unsurprising 
to find creatures of other natures that resemble them 
and are given their name—such as blink dogs and 
death dogs.
Blink Dog
A blink dog takes its name from its ability to blink 
in and out of existence, a talent it uses to facilitate 
its attacks and to avoid harm. These fey spirits are 
thought to have taken on an appearance resembling 
canines in order to foster a relationship with other fey 
that mimics the bond between people and their dogs. 
Blink dogs are exceptionally loyal to other fey and to 
each other, and fervently defend the territory of their 
companions.

Death Dog
A death dog is a two-headed hound that roams plains 
and deserts. Hate burns in a death dog’s heart, and a 
taste for flesh drives it to attack travelers and explorers. 
Death dog saliva carries a foul disease that causes a 
victim’s flesh to slowly rot off the bone. While some 
think they are dogs corrupted by experimentation 
with foul blood or exposure to dark magic, others 
believe they are negative manifestations created by the 
spirits of dogs that were mistreated in life.

doppelganger.content:
Doppelgangers were spawned fully formed from the 
mind of Dreja, the Mother of all Monsters. With 
just one overwhelming drive—spreading chaos—
doppelgangers went out into the world to fulfill the 
instinct. 
the people
Doppelgangers in their natural form appear as tall and 
slender gray-skinned, hairless beings. They lack any 
apparent sex characteristics and have milky white eyes. 
Since they spend most of their time infiltrating 
other lineages, they mostly have no culture of their 
own. They are able to sense each other when using 
their mind-reading ability without any sort of 
detection.
Occasionally when a doppelganger has deemed 
they’ve sowed enough chaos in the world, they settle 
down somewhere and live life the best way they know 
how, sometimes as a complete new identity, sometimes 
taking on the identity of someone they’ve shapeshifted 
into. When this happens, other doppelgangers tend 
to be drawn to them, at least for a time, before 
going back out into the world. Other times, a weary 
doppelganger tries to find the Mother of all Monsters 
and have her absorb them back into her.
doppelGanGer template
This template can be applied to any person stat block. 
They keep their statistics, except as noted below.

usually increases by 1. To be certain, recalculate the

their type.

they have seen, or back into their true form. Their 
statistics, other than their size, are the same in each 
form. Any equipment they are wearing or carrying 
isn’t transformed. They revert to their true form if 
they die.
D

dragons.content:
Dragons are intelligent, winged reptilians of ancient 
origin. A standout characteristic is their ability to 
breathe fire or other destructive energy, laying waste to 
entire armies of those who dare oppose them. Dragons 
can live hundreds of years, with the most long-lived of 
them over a millennia old. Much of that time is spent 
in hibernation, usually in a cave or underground lair.
Dragons come in a staggering diversity of colors, 
suggesting several different types. But dragons are 
all one kind. Their color is a mere environmental 
adaptation to camouflage them from their enemies 
and prey. Within a year of migrating to a new 
environment, a dragon grows new scales under 
its old ones, which then flake off. During this 
transformation, it’s not uncommon to hear reports of 
a dragon of one color with large patches of another 
color showing through. The adaptation is not only 
scale-deep, as dragons may grow or lose webbed claws, 
horns, gills, and more. Swapping one breath weapon 
for another is yet another adaptation.
Each dragon is an individual, evincing a wide array 
of disposition and personality among dragonkind. 
Some are craven and crafty while others are gregarious 
and sociable. Those who live near people and are so 
inclined learn to change shape to move freely among 
cities, villages, and tribes.
Variant Trait: Change Shape
An ancient or adult dragon that lives near settlements or 
other sizeable groups of people adds the following trait to its 
stat block:
Change Shape. The dragon magically polymorphs into a 
person that has a challenge score no higher than its own, or 
back into its true form. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Any 
equipment it is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the 
new form (the dragon’s choice).
In a new form, the dragon retains its health pool, Health Dice, 
ability to articulate, proficiencies, Legendary Resistance, lair 
actions, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Presence, as well as this 
action. Its statistics and capabilities are otherwise replaced by 
those of the new form, except any step features or legendary 
actions of that form.
D

dragonborn.content:
The dragonborn were breathed into life by Ulruth 
and Ayraed at the same time as the kobolds and 
dragons in a time when they weren’t enemies bound to 
destroy each other. The dragonborn and kobolds were 
originally created to aid the dragons in their grand 
plans for the world, and for a time the dragonborn 
followed that path, dedicating their lives to the whims 
and goals of their dragon overlords.
However, as time went on it was clear that the 
dragons’ goals and whims were petty things or 
completely disregarded their lives. The different 
dragonborn clans banded together, and either through 
words or blood, left the service of the dragons to live 
life as they saw fit. When they left the dragons, they 
also turned their backs on the gods that created them 
to be subjugated and left them in the clutches of such 
petty and uncaring beings.
The People
Dragonborns look like the humanoid form of their 
previous masters. They are covered in scales of a 
variety of colors. Most of them don’t have tails, but 
some do. They have talons on their hands and feet.
Clan before everything else. That is the core tenet of 
being a dragonborn. In all their dealings, dragonborns 
remember that their deeds reflect on all those that 
share their clan names. The greatest affront is to do 
something that shames their clan. 
The majority of dragonborns spend their lives inside 
dragonborn havens where their customs are the norm. 
The dragonborn who live outside are often diplomats, 
adventurers, or exiles. Those who make a life outside 
oftentimes still believe in the ways of their people and 
follow all of the customs, even if they aren’t around 
others of their kind. The exception to that are exiles, 
and that depends on why they were exiled. 
Dragonborn Template
This template can be applied to any person stat 
block. The person keeps their statistics, except as 
noted below.
Tag. The dragonborn adds the dragonborn tag to 
their type.
Size. The dragonborn’s size is Medium.
Resistances. The dragonborn has resistance to 
a type of damage based on the color of their scales 
(choose or roll a d10): 1–2, acid (black, copper); 3–4, 
cold (silver, white); 5–6, fire (brass, gold, red); 7–8, 
lightning (blue, bronze); 9–10, poison (green).
New Action: Breath Weapon. The dragonborn 
can exhale destructive energy (but can’t do this more

creature in the area must make a saving check (DS 
= 8 + the dragonborn's Health + their proficiency 
bonus), suffering 2d6 damage on a failed check, or 
half as much damage on a successful one. The color of 
a dragonborn’s scales determines the damage type, area 
of effect, and saving check type.

dragon_turtle.content:
A mythical creature of the deep, the dragon turtle is 
as legendary as its winged cousins. These sea-dwelling 
draconic creatures resemble colossal turtles with 
mountainous shells—albeit with heads that resemble 
terrestrial dragons, colorfully scaled skin, and claws at 
the end of their flippers. As with other dragons, the 
color of their scales depends on their environment. 
In colder waters, their scales grow paler; in warmer 
climates, they become more vibrant. Those that dwell 
closer to the water’s surface have a metallic sheen to 
their scales; the deeper they lurk, the more desaturated 
and dark their scales appear.
As with other dragons, dragon turtles embody a 
wide range of personalities. Some collect treasure from 
sunken ships while others sink ships to acquire it. 
There are dragon turtles that only interact with aquatic 
people, and there are those that protect any person 
traveling the sea. Some seafaring communities have 
struck alliances with dragon turtles for protection, and 
other cultures make pilgrimages to seek the wisdom of 
ancient dragon turtles.

dryad.content:
Dryads are fey spirits, resembling sylvan, humanoid 
figures, inhabiting and personifying specific trees. 
While not every tree has a dryad, every dryad has a 
tree that their essence is bound to and their health 
depends on. Dryads dutifully strive to not only 
protect their tree, but the grove or forest in which that 
tree grows. As caretakers of nature, they make fast 
friends with the flora and fauna that surround their 
home. They are similarly friendly with other fey and 
eagerly help those that enter their grove or forest.
While they find people fascinating, dryads are shy 
and reluctant to interact with them. A patient person 
with respect for nature can befriend a dryad with 
persistence and kindness, earning them a devoted 
and generous ally. Dryads avoid violence if they can, 
but fight if their land—and especially their tree—is 
threatened. In striving for a nonviolent resolution, 
dryads first try to enrapture enemies to convince them 
to leave, but call upon the power of nature and their 
woodland allies if given no other choice.

dwarves.content:
Created from the stone of the earth by Thorfet, the 
Great Creator, and Azzirra the AllMother, dwarves 
have always been attuned with the earth, being able 
to easily and deftly find and manipulate all of its 
treasures.
The People
Dwarves are among the shortest of all the peoples, 
individuals standing between four and five feet tall. 
They come in every range of skin tones from the palest 
of whites to the darkest of browns. They typically have 
very kinky hair in shades of reds, browns, and blacks.

eagles.content:
An eagle is a sizable and powerful bird of prey. 
Their long, broad wings contribute to their swift 
aerial speeds, and their large, hooked beaks easily 
tear into prey. Eagles are known for their incredibly 
keen eyesight. They can be found in many different 
habitats, from dense woodlands to populated lakes to 
mountainous regions.
A giant eagle is a noble creature that understands 
speech. A mated pair of giant eagles typically has up 
to four eggs or young in their nest. Aside from their 
size and greater intelligence, giant eagles display 
habits similar to their smaller counterparts—though 
they hunt far larger creatures and nest at far higher 
altitudes.

elementals.content:
The fundamental, primordial elements that make 
up existence are air, earth, fire, and water. There 
are planes of existence that embody only one 
each, but also areas throughout the planes that 
resonate specifically with one of them. In these 
areas, elementals can form. These spirits are each 
manifestations of the primeval element that spawned 
them, living extensions of those forces that embody 
the element’s traits.
They interact with their environment and other 
creatures in accordance to those traits. For example, 
fire elementals can blaze with destruction or provide 
life-giving warmth, while water elementals can as 
easily drown travelers as they can rejuvenate and carry 
them to safety. Earth elementals cause landslides 
and provide shelter to wandering creatures, and air 
elementals create thundering squalls and slow the 
descent of plummeting people. While they carry 
within them the potential of primordial devastation, 
elementals also bear the nurturing aspects of their 
incarnate element.
A trained spellcaster can call upon the service of an 
elemental. Oftentimes, this practice is used to assist 
in combat or with another task befitting the specific 
elemental summoned—such as a fire elemental 
providing heat for a furnace or an earth elemental 
clearing a cave-in. Some spellcasters forcibly bind an 
elemental’s assistance, while others have found ways to 
entreat the spirits for aid without compulsion.

elemental_sprite.content:
Take a handful of raw elemental material and add an 
extra big dollop of mischief. That’s an elemental sprite. 
Born of the raw forces of the multiverse, these sprites 
are composed of wispy threads of one or more of the 
elements. Most are attuned to a basic element: fire, 
water, air, or earth. But the more versatile elemental 
sprites contain more than one.
When in their element, these sprites gleefully 
pull pranks on, frighten, and pester planar travelers. 
When in danger, they can channel the elements into 
a surprising attack that shocks, freezes, or burns their 
enemies.

elk.content:
Elks are one of the largest species of deer. They inhabit 
forested regions or areas bordering forests and are very 
social animals, forming large herds—especially during 
warm seasons. As with other deer, elks are prized for 
hunting, though certain cultures refuse to do so to 
avoid accidentally pursuing or angering a giant elk.
The majestic giant elk is rare to the point that its 
appearance is often taken as a foreshadowing of an 
important event, such as the birth of a monarch. 
Legends tell of gods that take the form of giant elk 
when visiting the Material Planes. Many cultures 
therefore believe that to hunt these creatures is to 
invite divine wrath.

elves.content:
Drow
After they were cast out by their elven brethren for 
being under the sway of their evil goddess, the drow 
lived with deception, intimidation, and oppression. 
Their goddess’s sway led them to the most terrible 
acts of depravity against their own and others. Slavery 
and murder were everyday parts of life until the great 
rebellion. The drow rose up against their leadership, 
no longer wanting to be bound to their goddess, no 
longer wanting the life of depravity they’d been forced 
to endure. 
In the end, many lives were lost, but the drow won 
their freedom. They left the cities where so much pain 
and cruelty occurred, starting new ones both on the 
surface and underground. Some did stay in the city 
and continued to worship the goddess, never knowing 
anything else and not wanting anything else.
The People
Drow typically have white or silver hair and darkened 
skin ranging from dark purple to obsidian black. Their 
eyes are red, gray, violet, or yellow. 
Those who abandoned their goddess scattered 
throughout the land, creating or joining new 
communities. There was some initial hostility, 
especially from communities that had been directly 
impacted by the drow’s previous behavior. But in time, 
that eased. 
The drow who live in mixed-ancestry communities 
either try to keep to themselves or be pillars of the 
community. They’ve abandoned all the cultural 
practices they once had and adopted the ones of their 
new community.
The drow who created new communities kept a lot 
of their cultural practices to still feel some connection 
to their roots but modified them to reflect their 
progress. Those who live in secluded areas are self-
sustained and try to stay out of sight of other groups 
of people. The ones that surfaced near others opened 
up trade, sending ambassadors and trying to be a part 
of the community at large.
Drow Template
This template can be applied to any person stat 
block. The person keeps all their statistics except as 
noted below.
Tag. The drow adds the elf tag to their type.
Size. The drow’s size is Medium.
Senses. A sighted drow gains darkvision out to a 
radius of 120 feet.
Fey Ancestry. The drow has advantage on saving 
checks against being enraptured, and magic can’t put 
them to sleep.
Innate Spellcasting. The drow’s spellcasting ability 
is Presence (spell save DS 11). They can innately 
cast the following spells, requiring no material 
components:
At will: dancing lights
1/day each: darkness, faerie fire
Sunlight Sensitivity. While in sunlight, the target 
of a drow’s attack has advantage on defense checks and 
the drow’s Wisdom (Perception) skill score suffers a −5 
penalty. Remove this trait if the drow spends a year or 
more living on the surface.

enforcer.content:
Enforcers are those individuals from different walks of 
life who are contractually hired or employed for duties 
that require physical strength or presence. While 
such jobs can be unscrupulous, such as intimidating 
shopkeepers for protection money or forcibly 
collecting overdue debts, there are many legitimate 
enforcement jobs, such as protecting merchant 
caravans or acting as bodyguards for public officials. 
Given enough time working together, enforcers learn 
how to best complement each others’ strengths, in 
combat or otherwise, to provide opportunities and 
efficiently handle situations.

ettercap.content:
Ettercaps are arachnid-like monsters. Much like 
spiders, ettercaps weave webs, using them to entrap 
prey and mark the boundaries of their colonies, 
and scale vertical surfaces with ease. Ettercaps form 
communities in dark habitats—underground tunnels, 
mountainous caverns, or gloomy forests—and 
communicate with chittering sounds and clicks.
As they find it difficult to communicate with other 
creatures, ettercaps normally keep to themselves. If the 
barrier of communication can be bridged, however, 
ettercaps with no reason to distrust outsiders often 
provide refuge for travelers in exchange for food 
or goods.

ettin.content:
Ettins are two-headed giants who wander the planes 
in search of their lost history. Each of the heads of an 
ettin has its own individual personality, though both 
control the body. While the two heads can dislike 
each other and struggle to coexist, more often than 
not, the ettins’ heads are lifelong companions—each 
other’s most steadfast ally and closest friend. Such a 
connection grants them flawless coordination; they 
watch over each other’s rests during the night and are 
more likely to remain in control when dealt a magical 
or physical blow to the head.
Ettins gather in loose communities around the 
world to trade goods and information, after which 
they depart, alone or in small groups, to continue 
wandering the realms. They seek the history of their 
people that was lost in past calamities, and in that 
pursuit ettins have learned vast and ancient lore. 
Ettins are significant sources of historical knowledge 
and eagerly trade information to travelers who have 
useful material goods or know anything about the 
ettins of old.

frogs.content:
Frogs are short-bodied, tailless amphibians with long 
tongues and skin whose coloration can range between 
muted to vivid hues. They have a wide range of 
habitats, from tropical to arctic regions, and typically 
dwell near water, in trees, or underground. As 
carnivores, frogs feed on insects. They are able to leap 
significant distances. Giant frogs occur in areas with a 
high exposure to magic and, if threatened, engage in 
combat, unlike their smaller relatives. If its prey or an 
opponent is small enough, a giant frog doesn’t hesitate 
to swallow it whole.
Toads are a subspecies of frogs known for their dry, 
leathery skin covered in bumps, shorter legs, and a 
preference toward less aquatic habitats. Giant toads 
fight similarly to giant frogs, but are overall more 
dangerous because of their greater durability and 
poisonous bite.

fungi.content:
Fungi are found throughout the Material Planes 
and grow by feasting on dead matter, ideally in dark 
and moist conditions. However, when fungi grow 
in regions awash with heavy magic or from feeding 
on deceased magical creatures, they can develop 
sentience and cultivate new and unusual properties. 
These magical mushrooms are often indistinguishable 
from their nonmagical counterparts until aggravated. 
Two of these fungi are known as shriekers—named 
for the unbearable sound they emit in the presence 
of creatures or light—and violet fungus—who have 
limited mobility and can rot the flesh of creatures 
they touch.

Despite its appearance, the gargoyle is neither an 
animated object nor a living construct. They are, 
in fact, a statue animated by an elemental essence

genies.content:
Genies are mature primordial spirits that were once 
mere elementals. After centuries of unique experiences 
with other creatures, an elemental can manifest a 
more physical form and greater intelligence. These 
powerful elemental spirits—now genies—roam 
beyond the boundaries of the realms that bore them 
to collect greater and wider things. While some genies 
eventually tire of roaming and return to a primordial 
realm to make their permanent residence, others never 
settle and instead partake of the hospitality of the 
world for as long as they can.
Ancient sorcerers long tried to bind genies to 
their service, and some have never forgotten that 
transgression. Those genies nurse a contempt of 
mortalkind and either refuse to help people or are 
outright hostile toward them. Genies are capable 
fighters and spellcasters in their own right, and fight 
with guile and creativity. When a genie dies, it returns 
to the elemental energy that spawned it, leaving 
nothing but its material possessions as its spirit rejoins 
the elemental force.
Djinn
Djinn are genies manifested from air elementals. They 
are swift creatures, with lightning-fast movements and 
the power of storms at their command. As collectors, 
djinn roam the world searching for unique, priceless 
treasures—keeping their favorites and trading others. 
Their homes are typically found at the heights of the 
world, in permanently stormy regions, or atop the 
very clouds. Djinn put their collections on display 
and earnestly show them off and detail their history to 
interested parties. A person seeking a boon or one of 
a djinni’s treasures should bring something one-of-a-
kind as a gift of courtesy or to trade.

ghost.content:
At its death, the soul of a creature generally passes on 
to an afterlife in another realm. However, those souls 
fraught with business left unfinished may manifest 
upon the Material Planes as ghosts. These spectral 
figures haunt people, places, or possessions while 
seeking some resolution to the emotions that keep 
them bound to the world.
Ghosts have a varied awareness of their 
circumstances—ranging from complete clarity to 
uncontrolled fury to utter ignorance. Supernatural 
happenings occur in a ghost’s wake, terrifying nearby 
creatures and sending residents begging for aid. Those 
who seek to end a haunting could destroy the ghost, 
but even the most enraged spirit can be placated by 
resolving its unfinished business. Passing along a 
message, meting out justice, or convincing a ghost of 
its own death are just a few of the ways a ghost can be 
sent peacefully on.

ghouls.content:
Ghouls are ferocious undead created when the soul 
of an unintelligent beast is bound to the corpse of a 
mortal person by means of necromantic magic. Near-
feral creatures that lurk the boundaries of graveyards 
and battlefields, ghouls readily feast upon corpses and 
make new meals out of unsuspecting victims that draw 
too close to their feeding grounds. They fight with 
teeth and claws—the latter of which are infected and 
seizes creatures afflicted by them.
If a monster’s soul is used in the process to create 
a ghoul, the corpse instead rises as a ghast. More 
powerful than a ghoul, a ghast is surrounded by 
a sickening aura and exerts influence over ghouls, 
creating packs. A pack of ghouls are deadly scavengers, 
and the presence of a ghast makes them far less 
susceptible to divine rebuke.

giants.content:
The statuesque giants are a timeworn people whose 
civilizations once sprawled across the Material Planes 
and beyond. Vast calamities and sweeping wars 
shaped the realms and brought the giants down from 
the height of their empire. In their wake, they left 
numerous monolithic cities and fortresses as little 
more than abandoned ruins, rich with history to be 
discovered by today’s civilizations.
Yet the giants persist in the remote regions of 
the world. A people united in soul but divided by 
bloodlines; each giant’s lineage has an affinity to 
a force of nature—from the fury of storms to the 
arctic cold to the rolling hills themselves. While they 
were once a people of disparate nations, the giants 
came together to ensure their ways and traditions 
survived. Their communities vary between reclusivity 
for preservation, animosity toward smaller folk for 
supplanting the giants, and earnestness to welcome 
and share their culture with other people. Other 
giants have taken to the world to search the ruins of 
their ancestors and uncover anything they can use or 
preserve.
Cloud Giant
From their affinity with the stormless sky, cloud 
giants are blessed with innate magic through their 
bloodline. Drawing upon that magic, they can fly 
with ease, summon rolling fogs, transform their own 
bodies into mists, and even influence the weather. 
While cloud giants are well-known for their peaceable 
temperament, their patience isn’t without limits. Even 
clear skies can portent an overcast day.

people. Their bloodline has affinity to the fire 
that blazes beneath the earth, and their skin has a 
natural protective layer that prevents them from

giant families are notable smiths—not only crafting 
necessities for giant communities but their own 
elaborate armor and weapons.

The centipede is a carnivorous creature with a 
segmented body and many legs—sometimes 
up to several hundred—and are found almost 
everywhere. Normally their body is a ruddy color, but 
subterranean variants lack coloration and tropical ones 
are bright-hued. While a centipede is small enough to 
cause no trouble to a person, as even their venomous 
bite is only a painful irritant, giant ones that have 
developed in magical regions are a greater problem. 
The venom of a giant centipede is potent enough to 
numb a weakened creature.

are omnivorous, eating plants, nectar, and fruits as 
well as other insects. Many wasp species are solitary, 
but others are social. While regular-sized wasps are 
a nuisance and annoyance, the giant variant can be 
deadly. Their enormous stingers carry an effective 
poison that debilitates injected creatures for a time 
after being stung. It is best never to disturb a wasp’s

No one is certain whether gibbering mouthers are 
what becomes of people who visit the sea between 
worlds or just one of the many horrors that lurks 
within its depths that ensures those who enter are 
never seen again. 
Gibbering mouthers are amorphous creatures that 
manifest mouths to bite, spit, and utter appalling 
sounds. The aberration’s babbling contains the screams 
of horrified people, unearthly wailing, and words in 
a meaningless eldritch tongue—all of which sends 
creatures that hear it into either confusion or shock. 
Their forms overtake the area around them, grasping 
and slowing anyone who draws near, and they

The glacial ram looks like an ordinary mountain 
sheep from a distance, but drawing closer reveals its 
monstrous size. Unlike ordinary rams, the glacial ram 
is carnivorous and almost person-like in intelligence, 
even speaking its own rudimentary language.
It has a large collar of snow white fur ringing 
its head atop a stocky light gray body. At its ankle 
joints, spikes protrude out the back, both to assist in 
climbing ice walls, as well as pinning down prey. A 
pair of curling horns are black at their base but fade 
to brilliant white at the tips. Its icy blue eyes seem to 
release small trails of steam.

gladiator.content:
Gladiators battle for the entertainment of raucous 
crowds. Some gladiators are brutal pit fighters who 
treat each match as a life-or-death struggle, while 
others are professional duelists who command huge 
fees but rarely fight to the death.

gnoll.content:
The origins of gnolls are shrouded in mystery. Some 
claim they were spawned from the carnage of a demon 
prince. Others believe they were created through 
magical experimentation on regular hyenas. No one is 
sure what the truth is, not even the gnolls, and while 
many would like to know, most gnolls don’t bother 
with such trivialities. All that matters is the here 
and now.
The People
Gnolls resemble large, upright hyenas. Their furs range 
from solid whites, browns, and blacks, to spotted 
with all three colors. They have dark brown eyes that 
look almost black and their manes tend to match the 
dominant color of their fur.
Gnolls, or hyenafolk as some call them, are a 
matriarchal society that don’t worship any gods. 
Femme gnolls fill the majority of leadership positions. 
While this is not something that is strictly enforced, 
it remains true for the vast majority of gnoll packs. 
In instances when the androgynous and masculine 
gnolls are in positions of leadership, they often have 
some sort of council from the femmes, either as their 
second-in-command or a council of femme elders if 
they are in charge of a large group.
Together, gnolls defend their lands and people, 
caring for the home and children, or travel to be 
envoys to other groups of people—gnoll and non-
gnoll alike.
Save for the envoys, a gnoll can easily spend their 
entire lives in the same place, growing up around 
the same people and starting a family where their 
children can continue the cycle. However, at a certain 
age, a gnoll can start to feel a kind of wanderlust 
and seek some grand adventure. Oftentimes femme 
gnolls, once they’ve finished their adventuring, settle 
down some place different than their birthplace while 
nonbinary and masculine gnolls return home, 
assuming they’ve survived being away.
When different packs of gnolls meet each other, 
there is a formal presentation of their people to 
each other and an exchanging of knowledge and 
information to help the groups continue their way 
of life. This ritual has been even known to happen 
between enemy groups as a sort of parlay before any 
true violence happens. To engage in any dishonest 
behavior during this time is to court the anger of one’s 
own pack, which can lead to exile or death.
Gnoll template
This template can be applied to any person stat 
block. The person keeps all their statistics except as 
noted below.
Tag. The gnoll adds the gnoll tag to their type.
Size. The gnoll’s size is Medium.
Senses. The gnoll adds smelling to their primary 
senses, and a sighted gnoll gains darkvision out to a 
radius of 60 feet.
New Action: Bite. The gnoll can attack with their 
bite, inflicting piercing damage equal to 1d4 + their 
Strength on a hit.

gnomes.content:
Gnomes believe they share an origin with dwarves, 
having emerged from the earth. However, their origins 
diverge slightly as gnomes specifically believe their 
ancestors were birthed from the gems the earth held. 
None are quite sure how true this is and even their 
current gods aren’t aware, as they were once mortal 
and elevated by the faith of their people.
The People
Much like dwarves, gnomes are among the shortest of 
all peoples. They’ve got plumb faces and prominent 
noses. Their skin tones typically range from tan to 
dark brown, their eyes are on the lighter side, and 
their hair is shockingly vibrant.
Much like the dwarves, gnomes are known for 
their great craftsmanship, specifically in regards to 
clockwork mechanism and constructs. Unlike the 
dwarves, they don’t create things to venerate a god, 
but simply to appease their own curious nature and 
one-up their friends.
Due to their competitive drive, large creation 
celebrations are held quarterly throughout the year 
with the winner being crowned the Monarch of 
Creation. The monarch is treated with the deference 
due to royalty until a new one is crowned. However, 
unless qualified to rule, their opinion on government 
matters is politely ignored.

horns. They are one of the first domesticated animals

Domestic goats are found throughout the Material

elevations. Their horns are useful weapons, and the 
subspecies of giant goats use them to dangerous effect,

goblinoids.content:
Bugbears, goblins and hobgoblins were created to be 
mighty warriors, generals, and spies for Krolzenor 
the Red General. Krolzenor wanted dominion over 
all the gods and peoples. A great war was fought and 
Krolzenor was defeated, in part by his own creation 
who didn’t want to die just so he could rule. Millennia 
passed and now the bugbears, goblins, and hobgoblins 
live their lives as they see fit.
The People
Bugbears resemble hairy, muscular, and overgrown 
goblins, often standing well over six feet tall. Their 
nose and claws resemble those of bears, but the claws 
aren’t sharp enough to be used as weapons.
They are solitary creatures. You’re unlikely to see 
bugbears in large groups unless they’ve been employed 
by others to work together. At most, they travel in 
groups of three, and when that happens, it’s often two 
parents and their child. Left to their own devices, they 
wander from place to place taking in the scenery and 
culture. 
Goblins are short, round-faced people with green 
skin. They have coarse, often short hair and their eyes 
are typically dark brown, nearly black.
They surround themselves with other goblins. 
A family often consists of grandparents, parents, 
siblings, and any children. While the majority of the 
families are goblins, it isn’t unusual to see adopted 
hobgoblins and bugbears among them. When living in 
a neighborhood made up primarily of goblins, it feels 
like one large extended family. 
Hobgoblins are large and muscled with fur-covered 
bodies. Their fur is often reddish-brown, gray, or 
orange. They’re, on average, around six and a half 
feet tall. 
They value order and a strict hierarchy. Their 
communities are structured as such and the day-to-
day lives are very orderly. Each hour some type of 
signal, usually a bell or drums, is heard throughout the 
community in order to keep them on schedule. They 
do have unstructured hours, typically after the work 
day. Hobgoblins who were raised in communities but 
move to mixed-ancestry communities take a while to 
acclimate to the change.

grimlock.content:
The ancestors of grimlocks were humans who made 
caves and tunnels their home. Like most creatures who 
live underground in the total dark for generations, the 
grimlock became pale and lost their sight. Grimlock 
are born without eyes and adapted to rely on their 
other senses to navigate their subterranean territory. 
They are mostly hairless as well.
The People
People sometimes tell scary stories of grimlocks, but 
grimlocks are no more deadly than their surface-
dwelling counterparts. They have the same mix of 
benevolence and malice as humans do. Grimlocks 
cultivate vast lichen and mushroom farms, fish in 
underground lakes and streams, and hunt beasts 
and monsters who live in the dark. Close quarters 
underground has made grimlocks more patient and 
familiar with each other than members of most other 
peoples. They tend to sit down and resolve their 
differences rather than let them boil over, since leaving 
the group to strike out on one’s own is usually fatal.

hags.content:
Whispered of as crones and witches, hags are said 
to be evil incarnate. Lurking in their dark lairs, they 
devour children, corrupt wayward women, and 
deceive and destroy anyone else. Daughters are warned 
to act properly and littles one to behave, lest they be 
snatched up by the hags of dark stories and cautionary 
tales. After all, no one wants to be as hideous as a hag, 
nor devoured in the woods. But these stories told of 
hags do not reveal the whole truth. 
People are frightened of hags—but not about what 
they claim. The truth is that hags are women who 
refuse to be complicit and quiet. They choose bargains 
with the fey and other powers, trading their “prized” 
beauty for strength, over being prey to the whims 
and desires of unjust and corrupt systems. Hags are 
apostates and rebels who undermine evil that goes 
unseen.
A hag shelters women abandoned and disgraced 
for wanting their own path, rescues children from 
uncaring households, and torments those who would 
make others suffer through their own deception. It 
cannot be said that some hags do not live up to their 
reputation, but the vast majority seek to right the 
injustices they first ran from, no matter the cost. 
Green Hag
Green hags make their homes in twilit woods and 
gloomy swamps near the towns and cities they seek to 
subvert. Their uncanny ability to mimic the sounds 
of animals and people allow them to disrupt hunters 
and heroes searching for them or the children under 
their protection. Green hags can make themselves 
invisible and almost untrackable, further confounding 
those who hunt them. While their illusory magic does 
not hold up to inspection, green hags can disguise 
themselves enough to buy supplies from towns or keep 
an ear to the plights of those they would seek to aid.
