halfdragon.content:
Half-dragons do not share the divine origins that 
the other draconic lineages do. They’re created from 
dalliances between polymorphed dragons and other 
creatures. Their worship of Ayraed and Ulruth vary 
widely depending on where they grew up, which 
parent they grew up with, and their dragon parent’s 
own attitude towards the draconic gods.
The People
Half-dragons resemble their non-dragon parent but 
have the scales of their dragon parent on various parts 
of their body. They can be clearly visible, covering 
more than half of their body, or barely visible, only 
appearing in discrete places. They can have sharpened 
teeth and claws, or even wings.
Half-dragons belong to two worlds. Some half-
dragons hide their heritage and try to blend in with 
their non-draconic heritage. Others embrace their 
draconic heritage and the ego that comes with it, 
thriving to become someone whose name strikes awe, 
fear, and respect.
Dragonborn. Those who know the history of 
the dragons and dragonborn would think there was 
animosity between the half-dragons and dragonborn, 
but most dragonborn hail them as cousins, and some 
half-dragons have found themselves welcomed into 
dragonborn clans.
Kobolds. Half-dragons are treated like royalty, 
especially if they are the child of the dragon the 
kobolds serve. They can live among the community 
and feel right at home, even if they are the tallest 
member there.

Halflings are the creation of a pantheon that set them 
upon the world and still watch and guide them to this 
very day. They are the youngest of all peoples, having 
appeared centuries after the others. 
The People
Halflings are often stout with rounded faces. Their 
skin tone is typically on the fairer side of things, but 
dark skin tones aren’t unusual. They’re the same size as 
gnomes and dwarves. 
Halflings tend to live a modest and peaceful life 
in majority-halfling communities. They farm, they 
build, and they trade with others as necessary. When 
halflings come of age, they are encouraged to leave 
their community and go explore the world to figure 
out where they belong.
Most often, after roughly a decade of exploring, 
halflings settle down in the halfling community 
they were originally from or join new ones. In other 
cases, they’ll settle down in communities with other 
peoples. And in even rarer cases, they never give up 
adventuring.

Harpies were born fully formed from the mind of 
Dreja, the Mother of all Monsters. Created with a 
curious nature, they went out into the world to 
investigate people and things that enticed them.

barbed hair on their heads, legs, and long pointed 
ears. Otherwise, they look human.
A clamor of harpies consists of six individuals. They

hawk.content:
Hawks are diurnal birds of prey that hunt mammals, 
reptiles, and smaller birds. They can be found in most 
habitats, anywhere from forests and mountains to 
coasts and deserts. Hawks are known for their speed, 
especially while chasing prey, and are among the most 
intelligent of birds. Alongside falcons, hawks are one 
of the birds of prey trained for the sport of falconry.

These fiends are thought to either take the form of 
hounds or are created from the souls of slain death 
dogs. Within the lower realms, hell hounds are the 
prized companions of both devils and demons and 
loyally assist and defend their masters. Their hearts 
burn with an infernal fire that wreathes their fangs 
and that they can unleash in a devastating, fiery 
breath. Fiendish hound masters train packs of hell 
hounds to fight as a cohesive unit, as hell hounds 
fight better among allies, even if it is just their master. 
Despite their fearsome appearance, hell hounds are 
surprisingly playful when not in the midst of serious 
endeavors.

hippogriff.content:
The hippogriff is a creature with the front half of 
an eagle, including its wings, and the hind half of a 
horse. Its true origins are unknown, but some scholars 
speculate that the first hippogriff was born from the 
union between a griffon and a horse. Hippogriffs are 
notably swift fliers with an omnivorous diet, though 
they prefer to hunt unless prey is scarce. Similarly to 
griffons, hippogriffs are sought out as flying mounts—
however, they are much easier to train due to their 
equine lineage. Symbolically, hippogriffs are often 
depicted to represent unity and love.

horses.content:
Horses are hoofed mammals that have long been 
domesticated by people for use as mounts, workers, 
and companions. They are swift, terrestrial animals 
with a grazing, herbivorous diet. There are countless 
horse breeds throughout the Material Planes, often 
cultivated specifically for a certain kind of work. Draft 
horses are bred as working animals for farm labor, 
such as plowing or pulling carts of cargo. Riding 
horses are reared for speed and swiftness. Some horses 
H

humans.content:
The origin of humans is shrouded in mystery. They 
just appeared one day alongside the other peoples and 
quickly advanced societally.
The People
Humans vary wildly. They can have skin in all pale 
and earthen tones. Their hair ranges from the silkiest 
of blacks to the coarsest of blondes. Light to dark eyes 
aren’t uncommon, and their height is just as varied as 
their skin tone.
H

hydra.content:
There are few creatures that are as feared as the 
formidable hydra. These reptilian monsters are a 
scourge upon the regions they inhabit—swamps, 
lakes, coastlines, and other habitats near water where 
hydras make lairs in humid caverns. A hydra is born 
with five serpentine heads, a physical representation 
of its ravenous hunger. Should one of its heads be 
severed, a hydra is capable of not just regenerating its 
heads, but multiplying them, unless the stumps are 
cauterized before the process occurs.
Hydras are terrifying predators that dominate their 
territories, devouring any competition that tries to 
supplant them. They do not hesitate to lash out at 
prey with all of their heads, especially those that seek 
to flee. Unless prevented from doing so, hydras target 
the weakest prey in sight. If food becomes scarce, a 
hydra might turn upon its own heads for sustenance.

The hyena is a carnivorous mammal that is both a 
carrion scavenger and a pack hunter, with its behavior 
often dependent on its subspecies. It is found in 
habitats such as savannas, grasslands, woodlands, 
deserts, and mountains. Hyenas are notorious for 
their uncanny vocalizations that sound like laughter. 
As with many other beasts, giant hyenas can be found 
in areas saturated by magic. Packs of giant hyenas

invisible_stalker.content:
The process used by spellcasters to summon and 
bind elementals can be tailored for more specificity, 
depending on what task the summoner needs the 
elemental for. Invisible stalkers are elementals bound 
to be assassins. They are normally air elementals, 
though under certain circumstances—such as an 
aquatic environment or target—a water elemental 
can be used. To seal the binding, the spellcaster must 
provide the elemental a piece of its quarry, such as a 
drop of blood, a strand of hair, or a possession once 
on their person.
Once bound, the invisible stalker is connected to 
its prey—able to sense its location as long as they are 
on the same plane—and to its summoner in order 
to return to them. Invisible stalkers are typically 
unwilling servitors and must be forcibly bound. For an 
elemental to willingly submit to this kind of binding, 
they must agree that the creature the spellcaster 
wants hunted down deserves such a fate, even if their 
motivation differs from the summoner’s.

Jackals are canines and cousins to wolves and hounds. 
As opportunistic omnivores, jackals eat any food 
that is available to them—prey animals, carrion 
left by other predators, or flora and foliage. Jackals 
usually hunt and live in pairs, only gathering in larger 
packs to take down impressive prey or scavenge a 
particularly large carcass. They make their homes in 
savannas, grasslands, deserts, and other arid regions, 
and are most active at dusk and dawn.

kobold.content:
Kobolds share their origins with dragonborn but 
unlike them, the kobolds stayed close allies to the 
dragons, following the edicts of Ulruth and Ayraed. A 
few kobolds follow in the footsteps of the dragonborn, 
setting out on their own, but for the most part, 
kobolds stay near dragons while still living their 
own lives.
The People
Kobolds resemble dragonborn in a lot of ways: 
they’ve got the scales and draconic snout. But unlike 
dragonborn, all kobolds are smaller and have tails. 
Their scales can be as varied as dragons and the 
dragonborn, or they can be reddish brown and burnt 
orange.
They live their lives mostly in enclaves near dragon 
lairs. The enclave itself exemplifies communal living. 
The children are raised by everyone, and there are very 
few exclusive lovers in these enclaves. Everything a 
kobold does is expected to either help the community, 
or at the very least not put it in harm’s way.
When not attending to their own needs, the 
community assists the dragon they’ve committed 
themselves to. The things they do for this dragon 
can range from infiltrating other societies, hunting, 
exploring, and learning arcane and divine secrets. 
But no matter how much they revere the dragons 
and dedicate their lives to the ancient edicts of the 
draconic gods, they simply won’t risk the lives of 
their young.
The kobolds who either willingly leave the dragons 
or are forced out for one reason or another make their 
way to larger settlements to start new lives. If enough 
kobolds are in any given area, they tend to live near 
each other and emulate the communal living of the 
enclaves.
Kobold Template
This template can be applied to any person stat 
block. The person keeps all their statistics except as 
noted below.
Tag. The kobold adds the kobold tag to their type.
Size. The kobold’s size is Small.
Senses. A sighted kobold gains darkvision out to a 
radius of 60 feet.
Pack Tactics. The kobold imposes disadvantage on 
its target’s defense roll if at least one of the kobold’s 
allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn’t 
incapacitated.
Sunlight Sensitivity. While in sunlight, the target 
of a kobold’s attack has advantage on defense checks 
and the kobold’s Wisdom (Perception) skill score 
suffers a −5 penalty. Remove this trait if the kobold 
spends a year or more living on the surface.

kraken.content:
No creature is as feared by sailors as the dreaded 
krakens—legendary monsters lurking in the ocean 
depths. With crushing tentacles and a gaping 
mouth filled with rows of teeth, krakens prey upon 
seafaring vessels as easily as a wolf upon deer. They are 
territorial creatures and only rarely suffer intrusions in 
their domain above or below the waves. Sailors have 
countless superstitious rituals to keep krakens at bay—
from bardic shanties to warding tattoos to tossing 
specific herbs in the ocean—though only a few confer 
actual protection. 
Krakens have existed since the worlds were young, 
first shaped as weapons against an ocean deity and 
titan creatures of the sea. They easily wrest free of 
restraints, and their crushing power is such that they 
can capsize a boat in moments or lay waste to a port 
town if not adequately defended. From a primordial 
K

lamia.content:
Lamias were born fully formed from the mind of 
Dreja, the Mother of all Monsters, just like the 
doppelgangers and harpies. The ancestors of today’s 
lamias were disgusted by what they saw in other 
lamias and chose to strike out on their own and find 
places to isolate themselves.
the people
Lamias look half-person, half-lion or serpent. Their 
human half can appear as varied as regular humans. 
Their self-imposed isolation often leads them to 
ancient desert ruins, only meeting with other lamias 
in times of great peril or in order to mate and raise 
children. Because their diet consists almost exclusively 
of people’s flesh, they can enter a hibernative state 
K

lich.content:
The desire for immortality often plagues the mortal 
soul, especially those who are all too keenly aware 
of their own finite existence. For most, eternal life is 
little more than an impossible fancy. However, for 
transcendent spellcasters, it is perfectly within reach—
if one is willing to pay the price for it. Liches are 
the consequence of powerful mages using forbidden 
rituals to entomb their soul, and thus preserve it for 
eternity by willingly entering undeath.
Such secrets are difficult to find, and a would-be 
lich might scheme most of their mortal life to acquire 
the necessary rites from within ancient vaults or the 
hands of dark beings. Once they do, they have the 
means to contain their soul in a personal memento, 
then sacrifice their mortal form to rise as a skeletal 
lich. As long as the memento remains intact, a lich can 
return from any death—and so to destroy one, their 
soul’s receptacle must be destroyed. With eternity 
before them, liches spend years cultivating long-term 
designs to gather worldly power, magical items, or 
L

lion.content:
Lions are mighty felines—apex predators found in 
grasslands and savannas. They are social animals that 
gather together in groups known as prides. Male 
lions are noteworthy for their prominent manes, 
which the females lack. Lions are expert hunters; 
their remarkable bite force, claw strength, and leaping 
power all contribute to taking down their prey. These 
magnificent creatures are symbols of bravery and are 
often associated with courageous rulers. Some cultures 
tame lions to be steadfast companions to important 
figures.

living_constructs.content:
A living construct is a vessel, constructed in the shape 
of a person, to house a spark of life imbued by magic. 
Living constructs are not sentient, being created by 
spellcasters in order to carry out timeless duties, such 
as protecting a sacred place or town of innocents, 
on behalf of their creator. They differ from animated 
objects in that they are not merely enchanted to act 
and are not rendered inert by fields of antimagic. 
The strength of a living construct depends on the 
quality of material that goes into it, the proficiency of 
the artisan that crafts the vessel, and the skill of the 
spellcaster that imbues it with life. 
Clay and flesh are particularly fickle substances. A 
homunculus made of flesh is not only horrifying to 
behold, but also extremely vulnerable to fire. Both a 
homunculus of flesh and golem made of clay have a 
chance to go berserk if their vessel is damaged enough, 
as it puts the living construct’s magical spark in 
jeopardy. Though harder to procure and shape, both 
stone and iron are much more protective materials 
and make for sturdier constructs. All living constructs, 
due to the process used in their creation, are heavily 
resistant to magic and cannot have their forms altered 
by it. 
The magic that goes into creating a living construct 
also imbues it with magical strength and other 
abilities—such as surprising attacking speed in a 
golem or poisonous gas in an iron construct. While 
living constructs are imbued with the ability to follow 
instructions and carry out tasks, they are not intended 
to be individuals with consciousness. Some archmages 
have striven to change this, attempting to create living 
constructs with sentience, but such experiments are 
controversial.

lizards.content:
Lizards are widespread reptiles and can be found in 
every habitat throughout the Material Planes. They 
range in size from the span of a halfling’s finger to the 
length of a troll, not counting the giant subspecies 
typically found in magical jungles and in subterranean 
habitats. Lizards are generally carnivores, though 
some species are known to be omnivores or even 
herbivores. They have countless deterrents against 
predators—from venom to camouflage to sacrificing 
and regrowing their own tails. A giant lizard can be 
ridden or used as a draft animal. Subterranean giant

lizardfolk.content:
Lizardfolk see themselves as the oldest of all peoples, 
having always existed in the swamps of the worlds 
before any others walked them. With their history 
being a completely oral one, there are no documents 
to research to discover their origins.
The People
Lizardfolk are reptilian, like dragonborn and kobolds. 
They have scales all over their body, ranging in colors 
of dark green to shades of brown. They’ve got a long 
tail with spikes along it. The frill on their head looks 
like hair in a mohawk.
Lizardfolk society is ruled by the strongest. 
Challenges are frequently issued to change what the 
hierarchy looks like. Mundane challenges that have 
nothing to do with the leadership of a tribe can be

elemental essence within a body of magma. They are 
one of the easier elemental creatures for a spellcaster 
to summon, as only a sliver of an elemental spirit is 
called upon. Magmin are mischievous creatures, and 
rather careless with their ability to set things on fire—

mammoth.content:
A mammoth is an elephantine creature with thick 
fur and long tusks. Stockier and fiercer than normal 
elephants, mammoths inhabit a wide range of climes, 
from subarctic to subtropical. They are herbivorous, 
with a varied diet of shrubs, grasses, and herbs, and 
gather in small herds. Mammoths are immensely 
strong—their tusks are dangerous and lengthy 
weapons, and if a mammoth is allowed the space to 
charge, a foe can find itself trampled underfoot.

manticore.content:
Manticores are feared creatures, not foremost because 
of their formidable lion’s body or spined tail, but 
because of their person-like head. The resemblance is 
ghoulish on account of a manticore’s gaping mouth, 
filled with three rows of sharpened teeth—perfect 
for devouring the creatures they consider prey, which 
includes people. Manticores are capable of speech, 
and while many use it to unsettle their prospective 
meals, some communicate peacefully with mortal 
communities rather than consider them food. 
Their teeth and claws are deadly, but a manticore’s 
most versatile weapon is its tail. A manticore can shoot 
the spikes like arrows with frightening accuracy, even 
from a great distance, which they attain with their 
leathery wings. A manticore’s tail only has twenty-four 
spines on average, but they regrow after recuperating.

mephits.content:
A mephit forms when two different elemental forces 
coalesce in one spirit—a process that can happen 
naturally within the world and also if a spellcaster 
specifically sets out to summon one. Mephits are 
unpredictable elementals, as their personality is 
influenced by the combination of elemental essences 
that comprise them. They can be stubborn, fickle, 
fiery, tricksy, or any number of other mercurial traits. 
Mephits are noteworthy for their innate magic 
and elemental breaths, both of which can hinder 
foes or deliver a destructive barrage. A naturally 
formed mephit gravitates to habitats that resemble 
the elements they embody and can often blend into 
their environment because of it. As mephits are not 
particularly durable, they prefer to harass enemies 
from a distance or attack in numbers, and when they 
die, they erupt with explosive elemental energy.

merfolk.content:
Born from the essence of the ocean itself, merfolk 
are said to be as old as the waters they inhabit. If any 
recall the true origins, they keep it to themselves and 
espouse the tale that they simply came to be when the 
ocean did.
The People
Merfolk have skin the colors of ivory, silver, blue, 
and deep purple. They’ve got fins on the back of their 
forearms and legs. Their hands and feet are covered in 
webbing. Their hair is thick and frequently black.
They are torn between their desire to be the 
protectors of the ocean and giving into their 
wanderlust and living a nomadic life, exploring 
unknown depths. Large cities are erected in areas 
where other worldly incursions threaten those above 
and below the waves. The need to protect others have 
driven the merfolk to heroic deeds and villainous 
misdeeds.
When not engaged in battle, the life of city-bound 
merfolk mirrors that of a person on land. They do 
what they can to make sure their communities run 
smoothly, and that can include trading with topside 
fishers, merchants, and pirates.
Nomadic merfolk tend to travel in small groups of 
three to five people as they explore the ocean. While 
they do interact with the city-dwelling merfolk, it’s

merrow.content:
Merrow dwell in deep, dark waters. From a distance, 
they resemble merfolk, but the differences are clear up 
close. A merrow has a shark’s head filled with jagged 
teeth and crested by fins and spines, and hands with 
long, vicious claws. Merrow are skilled carnivorous 
predators, preying not only on smaller fish but also on 
larger aquatic creatures, which they hunt with guile or 
alongside fellow merrow.
Their natural weapons are dangerous, but merrow 
have also adapted to using harpoons scavenged or 
bartered from merfolk to better take down their prey. 
Merrow infrequently venture into lighter waters or 
near land—only when there is a scarcity of resources 
or food. While many merrow opt for violence to solve 
shortages, others have found more success in engaging 
in diplomacy with merfolk and surface dwellers to 
find aid.

Mimics are carnivorous creatures that find any meat 
palatable, and so to ambush unsuspecting prey they 
lurk in dungeons and similar environments, disguised 
as objects tempting to touch. While transformed,

minotaur.content:
The first minotaurs were trusted guardians of secrets 
and treasure in the realms of the fey. Some of their 
descendants remain in the employ of powerful fey 
lords and ladies, but most have sought out their 
livelihood elsewhere.
The People
Minotaurs stand head-and-shoulders taller than the 
tallest people. They have bovine faces, horns, and 
fly-swatting tails. Their most remarkable feature is 
invisible, the ability to perfectly recall any path they 
have taken. As such, they make natural guides, scouts, 
and explorers.
On the Material Planes, minotaurs often live 
in remote places, building small communities of 
minotaurs and those friendly to them. Their ability 
to find their way back home allows them to live 
in the most trackless places. Most who enjoy the 
hospitality of minotaurs never find their way back for 
a return visit.
Minotaurs’ stature makes them formidable 
opponents, and those who choose the soldier, warrior, 
or mercenary life are usually successful. Just as many 
minotaurs have a gentle disposition, content to 
ruminate about the multiverse and its many wonders.

mummy.content:
Under the right conditions—whether due to magic, 
the right environment, or the ancient embalming 
arts—the corpse of a person or beast can be preserved 
as a mummy. The process of mummification can be 
incidental or a deliberate cultural act performed after 
a creature’s death. When a mummy is intentionally 
made, the organs are removed and the body is 
carefully embalmed, wrapped, and sealed away.
Due to their unique preservation, mummies are 
especially resistant to being raised by necromancy. 
As such, spellcasters invested in the necromantic arts 
have devised a ritual specifically to raise mummified 
corpses. While magic animates the bodies—whose 
knowledge, skills, and magic they knew in life are 
also preserved—it has the unintentional side effect of 
cursing the undead creatures with a debilitating gaze 
and a malignant curse, one they could pass to others 
and would turn its victims to dust if not removed. 
Given the extensive rituals needed to raise one, 
mummies are rare. Their potent abilities and 
intelligence make them advantageous guardians, or 
even consultants, for the spellcasters who are able 
to create them, though few mummies relish their 
undead fate.
Mummy Template
This template can be applied to any beast or person 
stat block. The creature keeps all its statistics, except as 
noted below.
Type. The mummy’s type is undead.
Armor Scraps. The mummy’s defense score is 12 + 
its Agility.
Speed. The mummy loses any flying or swimming 
speed, and its speed is 20 feet.
Abilities. The mummy’s Strength increases by 3, 
and its Agility decreases by 1.
Saving Checks. The mummy gains proficiency in 
Wisdom saving checks.
Vulnerabilities, Resistances, and Immunities. 
The mummy gains vulnerability to fire damage; 
resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing 
from nonmagical attacks; and immunity to necrotic 
and poison damage and the enraptured, exhaustion, 
frightened, inert, and sickened conditions.
Senses. The mummy’s primary sense is sight, and it 
gains darkvision out to a range of 60 feet.

+ their proficiency bonus) or be cursed with mummy

and its health pool depth decreases by 10 (3d6) for
every 24 hours that elapse. If the curse destroys the
target’s health pool, the target dies, and its body turns
to dust. The curse lasts until removed by the remove
curse spell or other magic.
New Action: Dreadful Glare. The mummy targets 
one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. If the target 
can see the mummy, it must succeed on a Wisdom

the target fails the saving check by 5 or more, it is also 
inert for the same duration. A target that succeeds on 
the saving check is immune to the Dreadful Glare of 
all mummies for the next 24 hours.

nagas.content:
Many believe the naga came from the sea—legends say 
that the long-living creatures were the first to come 
from its waters, exploring the unmapped lands of the 
early worlds and seeking to understand the magic 
inherent in them. Much of that history has been 
lost to time; nowadays, what is known of the naga is 
that they are deeply magical. These ancient creatures, 
which bear people’s heads atop their long, serpentine 
form, are found in the deepest parts of ruins and 
wildernesses, where they guard, seek, or manipulate 
arcane secrets.
The nagas’ ability to return to life after they are 
slain is what makes them keepers of some of the most 
ancient of secrets. They are cunning spellcasters whose 
venomous bite is a last resort to protect themselves. 
Immensely solitary and secretive creatures, it is rare 
to find one, let alone a group. Many people who 
encounter a naga, however, come back knowing a 
once-buried occult secret—whether for good or for 
gravely ill.

nightmare.content:
Horses ridden by dark masters may find their souls 
carried to the lower planes, borne by the deeds of their 
owner. However, their fate proves advantageous, since 
such an equine is given the powers of a nightmare—a 
fiendish steed wreathed in flames. Nightmares are 
the loyal mounts of demons and devils, able to fly on 
currents of fire even faster than their new masters can 
bear themselves on great wings. A nightmare can also 
travel across the planes uninhibited, bearing its rider 
and their allies into realms ethereal.
While known as the loyal steed of fiends, 
there are legends of mortals proving themselves 
worthy to mount a nightmare. Nightmares respect 
an unyielding, relentless soul, impassioned by 
conviction—and people who embody those traits can 
earn a nightmare’s loyalty and ride the creature as they 
carry out their journeys.

The octopus is an aquatic creature with a soft, flexible 
body and eight tentacles. They make their habitats 
throughout the ocean, from the abyssal depths, 
coral reefs, and shallower waters. To avoid predators, 
octopuses can expel ink like a smokescreen and 
dart away and can also change the color and texture 
of their skin to blend in with their surroundings. 
Octopuses prey on mollusks and crustaceans for food. 
Giant octopuses are common in waters tinged with 
magic and can be mistaken for krakens by especially 
nervous and jittery sailors.

ogre.content:
Possessing herculean strength and incomparable 
courage, ogres are known in nearly every land. Their 
impenetrable fortresses of stone are often built into 
mountains and landscapes for stability and strength, 
providing an additional tactical advantage against 
any would-be enemies. There are some who claim to 
have seen the heart of the ogre fortresses and found 
immaculately preserved history—a hint that, perhaps 
like their giant kin, ogres seek and preserve some of 
the world’s oldest sites.
When threatened, ogres are martial masters of 
the greatclub and the javelin, allowing them to be 
dangerous both up close and at range. They are more 
dangerous in groups, protecting their weakest and 
picking off the easiest prey together. They respect 
shows of strength when seeking alliances or accepting 
connections—the cowardly are simply not worth 
their time.
O

oni.content:
The wise, wayfaring, yet imposing oni lost their 
homeland long ago to an ancient evil. These horned 
giants have an innate connection to the magic of the 
world, and so despite their lost lands, they find a 
home wherever the arcane is strong. Oni are colorful 
giants, with skin tones ranging from the common red, 
blue, and green to the much rarer black and yellow, 
and are otherwise notable for their clawed hands and 
prominent teeth.
Oni wander the realms searching for arcane lore, 
mystical secrets, and sagacious wisdom. They recognize 
their appearance is fearsome and that their stride is 
often too large for smaller people to match, so they 
use their innate talent to shapechange and take on 
the appearance of smaller mortals. Oni appreciate the 
hospitality of communities and enjoy conversations, 
but especially with elders and spellcasters, seeking to 
exchange what they know for new knowledge. While 
some oni use their abilities for deception and violence, 
most deeply respect other creatures and protect those 
who aid them and fellow travelers should they come 
to harm.

orc.content:
The old tales passed down from generation to 
generation claim that the orcs were born from two 
prime deities, Nar the Patient and Murbol the 
Ironfisted, who were enemies turned lovers turned 
enemies turned lovers, and so on until the end and 
restart of time. It is said that each time the pair 
became lovers new gods were created, and these gods 
in turn created orcs in their own image.
the people
Orcs and half-orcs can come in all shades of green or 
range from pale-skinned to dark. On average, they’re 
one of the taller peoples. Their hair is typically dark, 
and they have brown eyes to match it. 
Of all the orc clans, some of the most well known 
are the Howling Fang, Moon Scar, Iron Crag, and 
Crimson Stone.
Throughout most of the world, when the name 
Howling Fang is mentioned, there are mixed reactions. 
In one region they are a horde of marauders, killing 
and pillaging as they see fit. In another place, they are 
seen as valuable mercenaries. In yet another region, 
they are skilled warriors who have integrated into 
society and defend it with their lives.
The Moon Scar clan are the most spiritual of all the 
clans. Their fascination with the stars have led them 
to believe that they can glean the future from studying 
their movements. Their traditions are focused around 
astrology and ancestral worship, as they believe all 
the great members of their clan are immortalized in 
the stars.
The Iron Crag merchant clan is always traveling 
across the world, building relationships between 
various people. One notable relationship between the 
Crimson Stone clan has led to the creation and 
distribution of rare and powerful weapons, created 
from a rare metal that only the 
O

orca.content:
Orcas, known as the “wolves of the sea,” are large 
carnivorous marine hunters. Grouped in pods, they 
hunt everything from fish to walruses, and even 
stranger creatures—merfolk are known to be wary 
of orca pods, particularly in areas where fish are 
scarce. Orcas rip and tear into their prey with their 
teeth after sneaking up on schools of fish and other 
marine animals by blending in with their unique 
black-and-white coloration. They are primarily found 
in colder waters near coasts. Fishers and sailors near 
orca territory fear black dorsal fins rising from below. 
Orcas may tolerate nearby merfolk and other aquatic 
people so long as the orcas are well-fed, and some of 
the ocean’s greatest warriors are even said to use orcas 
as steeds.

Aberrations have no true sentinel, but the otyugh are 
close—a large, eerie vanguard. They are often still or 
slow-moving throughout the sea between material 
worlds, communicating through the haunting mind-
songs of their telepathy. However, these squid-like 
ambush predators are chilling when they strike. Their 
crushing tentacles and gaping maw mean that, at the 
first sign of disturbance or threat, they can attack, 
grapple, and consume in a matter of seconds.

owls.content:
Owls are nocturnal birds of prey known for their 
keen eyesight, sharp talons, and telltale hoot. Found 
throughout the Material Planes—aside from the most 
extreme climes—owls hunt small mammals, other 
birds, and insects. As owls have no peripheral vision, 
they can turn their heads nearly all the way around in 
order to view their surroundings. They are silent, agile 
fliers and can swiftly escape from predators without 
reprisal. Giant owls often befriend fey and other 
sylvan creatures and are guardians of their woodland

owlbear.content:
The unique growling hoot that disturbs the forest 
at night is the work of none other than the iconic 
owlbear, a creature known for its territorial aggression 
and terrifying strength. Its bulky, muscular ursine 
body bears both fur and feathers, while its head 
resembles an owl’s—though with a serrated beak that 
tears through prey with ease. The owlbear prowls 
its territory to hunt living creatures, both predators 
and prey alike, when the moon is high. Very few 
can take down a rampaging owlbear on their own—
coordinated efforts are often required to fend off this 
near matchless creature, but one that is befriended and 
tamed is a fearsome companion.

panther.content:
A silent, cunning hunter whose dark pelt allows them 
to disappear in the night, panthers have been likened 
to ghosts of the forest. They are predatory felines who 
are typically solitary and fiercely territorial. Panthers 
can be found in varied habitats, but especially in 
dense rainforests and other woodlands where they 
excel at climbing trees. From such vantages, panthers 
are known to pounce with deadly strength onto their 
prey, which includes small creatures such as birds 
and rabbits, as well as larger mammals like deer and 
primates.

pegasus.content:
Soaring above the clouds, the pegasus is the very 
picture of grace—a celestial horse borne aloft on 
immaculate wings. These creatures are the seraphic 
steeds of both gods and other celestials and carry their 
preeminent riders across both the heavenly and the 
Material Planes. Pegasi are loyal to their riders and 
keep a watchful eye out for their safety, using their 
hooves as a fearsome weapon to defend them if they 
should be endangered.
Though pegasi are known as celestial steeds, they 
are frequently sought out for their swiftness and 
temperament by mortal adventurers. Should one prove 
to a pegasus to be valorous and compassionate, the 
creature can forge a steadfast bond with that soul and 
willingly bear them across the world.

piranhas.content:
A piranha is a carnivorous, freshwater fish with sharp, 
triangular teeth meant for tearing meat off prey. While 
their typical diet consists of smaller fish, insects, and 
snails, piranhas opportunistically attack injured, 
larger beasts. When food is scarce and piranhas are 
starving, they are driven into a frenzy by the taste of 
blood in the water. Piranhas can adapt to any aquatic 
environment, including cold subterranean lakes. They 
frequently gather in swarms to protect themselves

priest.content:
Priests bring the teachings of their gods to the 
common folk. They are the spiritual leaders of temples 
and shrines and often hold positions of influence in 
their communities. Evil priests might work openly 
under a tyrant, or they might be the leaders of 
religious sects hidden in the shadows of good society, 
overseeing depraved rites. A priest typically has one or 
more acolytes to help with religious ceremonies and 
other sacred duties.

pseudodragon.content:
Curious and capricious, the pseudodragon is a feyborn 
creature resembling a miniature dragon. Some would 
claim pseudodragons are actual dragons, cursed by 
archfey for perceived slights, while others believe 
that they were crafted specifically by fey who sought 
dragons as pets and companions—but in a more 
manageable size. While pseudodragons cannot speak, 
they can impress their thoughts and feelings onto the 
creatures around them. 
Pseudodragons are sought out as companions 
by eccentrics and adventurers for their uniqueness 
and resistance to magic, though their mercurial 
personalities are often underestimated. Unlike actual 
dragons, a pseudodragon’s scale color does not change 
based on their environment, but they can alter their 
own scale color according to their moods. To defend 
themselves, pseudodragons can inject opponents with 
a catatonic poison through a stinger at the end of 
their tail.

psychic_worm.content:
Encountering a psychic worm is a mind-addling 
experience. The first telltale sign is a mucus trail that 
iridescently shimmers purple and green. To touch the 
mucus is to be immediately bombarded by psychic 
sensation, an overwhelming experience for most 
people. Coming in physical contact with a mucus 
trail alerts a psychic worm to your presence. In fact, 
the worm’s mucus-laden tunnel network acts as an 
external brain, and those interfacing with a worm’s 
mucus, especially other psychic worms, become part 
of the aberration’s neural network.
A psychic worm generally avoids a fight. Hunger or 
being hunted itself might compel a psychic worm to 
go on the offensive. A psychic barrage or two from 
the worm is enough to render most prey docile and 
insensate, easy food for a hungry psychic worm.

purple_worm.content:
When the earth rumbles with the gnashing of teeth, 
those who dwell below the earth’s surface know to 
flee. Voracious destroyers named for the hue of 
their plate-thick scales, purple worms bring 
ruin upon underground communities. 
These enormous monsters carve through 
solid stone as if it were mere dirt in 
pursuit of their next meal. The horrifying 
strength of a purple worm’s bite means it 
can easily tear a creature in half. Anything 
that survives is swallowed whole, and any 
other prey is made the victim of the deadly 
poison running through the worm’s stinger.
Purple worms have no eyes and rely on their 
hearing or their ability to detect vibrations through 
the earth to locate potential prey. Underground 
cities have developed methods to create sound or 
vibrations that lure purple worms away from their 
homes. Similar techniques can 
be used by more nefarious 
individuals to lure the 
colossal creatures to the 
surface, the arrival of 
which is heralded by a 
localized earthquake before 
the purple worm 
bursts from the 
earth and consumes 
whatever attempts to 
flee from its havoc.

rakshasa.content:
In a time long past, the rakshasa left the structured 
hierarchy of the lower planes. Neither devil nor 
demon, these fiends—notable for their bipedal tiger 
appearance, prominent fangs, and claw-like hands—
departed on a journey to understand what defines a 
mortal soul and its journey after death. Rakshasa are 
innately attuned to the magic of the universe in ways 
that few other creatures are. Not only does their own 
strength allow them to cast deceptive spells with ease, 
but they can manipulate magic in such a way as to 
remain unaffected by all but the most powerful spells 
cast upon them. It is rumored the rakshasa’s claws 
bring unending nightmares.
Rakshasa have long since dispersed across the 
planes, preferring to indirectly involve themselves 
in the affairs of mortals. Many in disguise have 
accompanied adventurers or advised benevolent 
rulers, all in pursuit of understanding the potential 
for goodness in a mortal soul. Others align themselves 
with villainous forces, testing and tempting heroes 
to see how far one must be pushed before their soul 
is consigned to the lower planes. While rakshasa 
typically rely on their cunning, those that befriend 
creatures or have plans they are desperate to keep in 
motion can prove to be dangerous foes that threaten 
what’s important to them.

rats.content:
The scurrying of rodents is a common sound wherever 
people gather. Rats are small mammals found 
throughout the Material Planes, but especially in 
the bustling hearts of civilization. As opportunistic 
scavengers, rats find it beneficial to be where people 
are, plucking their meals from the waste left behind 
by their larger neighbors. Rats make their homes in 
sewers, abandoned buildings, and other dark, remote 
areas. They are nocturnal, and use the cover of night 
to remain out of sight while finding food.
A rat’s teeth are strong enough to chew through 
wood and metal, with the infamous and vexing giant 
rats able to chew through even thicker materials. Rats 
are prone to carrying and passing on virulent diseases, 
and they often gather in swarms—which allow them 
to overwhelm enemies when they are antagonized. 
Plenty of fledgling adventurers are tasked with ridding 
local establishments of the nuisance of these oversized 
or congregating pests.

The black-plumed raven is often considered an ill 
omen—associated with death, lost souls, and poor 
fortune to come. While ravens are omnivorous, with a 
diet of nuts as well as other birds, they are best known 
and macabre for feasting on carrion. They are found 
in several habitats, from forests and mountains to 
deserts and tundras. Ravens are remarkably intelligent, 
holding grudges against creatures that earn their ire 
and bringing gifts to those they are fond of, and can 
mimic sounds they have heard. While a perceptive ear

remorhaz.content:
Considered significant dangers in arctic climates, 
remorhazes are great, burrowing worms that prowl 
the frozen fields. Their unique physiology allows 
them to shrug off extreme cold and to burn energy 
and nutrients as a fire that warms their body inside 
and out.
Remorhazes hunt primarily by burrowing beneath 
layers of snow and ice—which their scalding outer 
scales easily melt to make movement easier—and 
patrolling paths around their territory until they 
sense significant motion above ground. As they need 
a considerable amount of sustenance to keep the fire 
within their body alight, they do not bother with 
small prey unless starving. Travelers are cautioned to 
stay in small groups while traversing areas known to 
be patrolled by a remorhaz, or areas where the snow 
and ice is noticeably thinner than the surrounding 
region.

The mighty rhino is an immense mammal of 
significant size and weight—yet despite its fearsome 
appearance, a rhinoceros is a docile herbivore, content 
to graze on grass and plants. Found roaming grassy 
plains, rainforests, and swamps, rhinos are known for 
the horns that grow on their noses. They are easily 
startled and charge and trample the object of their 
fear. Because of their thick skin, rhinos have few 
bestial predators, though creatures such as hydras and 
dragons are not deterred by their natural defenses and 
consider them prey.

roc.content:
It is said that to find oneself in the shadow of a roc’s 
colossal wingspan is to know true terror. This bird 
of prey, resembling an enormous eagle, rivals the 
size of an ancient dragon. Rocs make their nests at 
the heights of small islands or in the mountains near 
coastlines. Due to their sheer size, a roc’s preferred 
method of hunting prey is to snatch large creatures, 
such as elephants or sharks, in their talons—then drop 
them from a great height. A roc rarely bothers to hunt 
small prey unless food is scarce or it’s angry.
As intelligent as a horse, the roc can recognize 
individual creatures and act accordingly. People 
who befriend a roc might find that they have an 
unexpected ally. However, nothing angers a roc more 
than their eggs being destroyed or stolen. Old tales 
speak of rocs that hunted such thieves across the sea—
sinking entire fleets as retribution for their lost young.

rust_monster.content:
Both a bane and blessing—though mostly a bane—
to miners, rust monsters are beetle-like creatures 
infamous for feasting on ferrous metals. Their body 
secretes a substance, concentrated in their antennae 
and chitinous shell, that rusts metal on contact, 
allowing them to more easily devour it. Rust monsters 
seek out their food of choice by scent. The metallic 
nature of their shells is a byproduct of their diet, and 
their sizable mandibles are useful weapons to bite 
through weakened metal armor.
Rust monsters typically dwell underground and 
converge in areas where ferrous ore is common. 
Miners often use nests of rust monsters to pinpoint 
where such metals are, after which they are promptly 
cleared out by capable warriors before mining 
operations begin. It is not unheard of for rust 
monsters to be captured and unleashed during sieges 
or as saboteurs, causing rampant destruction of iron 
armaments and basic tools.

sahuagin.content:
Like merfolk, sahuagin are also a people of the sea, but 
their origins are tied to the merfolk’s need to protect 
others at all cost. After a particularly dangerous war 
with an aboleth and their minions that decimated 
a number of merfolk towns and cities, a group of 
wizards concocted a spell that would transform 
willing merfolk into stronger versions of themselves. 
Hundreds volunteered and the first sahuagin 
were born.
Initially they did their duty well, giving their 
lives to protect their fellow merfolk, but eventually 
many sahuagin grew unhappy with how their lives 
were treated as expendable compared to the merfolk 
warriors who hadn’t undergone the change. The 
sahuagin rebelled, killing the wizards who knew the 
spell to create more sahuagin and striking out on 
their own.
The People
Sahuagin are very muscular. They’ve got horns and a 
membrane all over their body, with spikes protruding 
from them. They’ve also got powerful spiked tails and 
dark black eyes.
Due to the way the merfolk treated them, they’ve 
viewed them as their most hated enemies. After the 
rebellion, there was a time when they would raid 
merfolk cities and towns for supplies and revenge. 
Because of these actions, the merfolk in turn saw them 
as hated enemies.
The sahuagin live a nomadic life, not by choice, 
but out of necessity. Despite the fact that they bear 
many children, sahuagin are outnumbered by merfolk 
almost ten to one, and whenever one group comes 
across the other, fighting ensues with devastating 
losses on both sides, but more so for the sahuagin.
Due to this bitter rivalry, it's common to find 
sahuagin communities on the coast or traveling among 
sailing ships.

armor, their defense is equal to 12 + their Agility 
bonus or penalty.

40 feet.

radius of 120 feet.

Perception skill.

don’t have a completely full health pool.

once every 4 hours to avoid suffocating.

limited telepathy.
New Action: Bite. The sahuagin can attack with

their Strength on a hit.
New Action: Claws. The sahuagin can attack with 
their claws, inflicting slashing damage equal to 1d4 + 
their Strength on a hit.

From the darkest and neglected corners of the 
subterranean world, the saknid was birthed from 
a cesspool of vile liquid that slowly collected from 
the drippings of decomposing creatures, cursed 
abominations, and anything else that trickled its way 
into its retched puddle. The saknid evolved and grew 
quickly by draining the life essence and withering the 
matter of anything it finds in its path, alive or not.
Driven only by feeding its hunger and the primal 
urge to provide sustenance to its larvae that squirm 
about the necrotic black ooze that permeates its nest, 
the saknid uses its natural camouflage and powerful 
abilities to ambush anything that stumbles into 
its hunting ground. Armed with its long chitinous 
exoskeleton, stunning barb-covered legs, and a fang-
filled pharynx that protrudes from its maw, the saknid 
quickly incapacitates and devours its prey. The saknid’s 
stomach maintains a magic portal to its nest and can 
choose to send its prey directly to its nest for its spawn 
to feast upon.

salamander.content:
Salamanders are elemental beings that resemble 
massive versions of the beasts that share their name—
they are lizard-like, with short limbs and long tails. 
A salamander is born under unusual circumstances, 
emerging from the flames set by a fire elemental. Their 
reptilian scales radiate a scorching heat that heats or 
burns anything that touches them. As such, they shy 
away from physical contact with creatures that aren’t 
resistant to fire and have found distant ways to greet 
and show affection and gratitude to other people.
Having an aversion to the cold, salamanders prefer 
to dwell in hot climates, where they wander or find 
hospitable communities. Oftentimes, salamanders aid 
travelers or villages and towns with tasks that require 
heat in exchange for supplies or other aid. To defend 
themselves, salamanders use long weapons, like spears, 
to make up for their short reach, or use their tails, 
which have a crushing grip.

satyr.content:
Boisterous and vibrant fey, satyrs are recognizable 
for having the upper body of a person, usually one 
seemingly elven; the lower body of a goat; and 
noticeable horns. They are infamous for revelry and 
indulgence; folk tales and stories regale of the lavish 
feasts, extravagant parties, and outrageous productions 
that satyrs host in the woodlands. While other fey 
are their common guests—for satyrs love bringing 
entertainment to their peers—it is not unheard of 
for them to invite mortals, especially those they’ve 
befriended.
Satyrs are also said to sneak into celebrations, such 
as a city’s festival or a village’s harvest feast, and bring 
their own food and drink as a gift. Some satyrs delight 
in causing mischief with their escapades, but others 
merely want to experience all that the Material Planes 
have to offer, and then there are those satyrs who want 
to share entertainment and pleasures with everyone 
they meet—to lift spirits and bring hope to those who 
need it.

scorpions.content:
Scorpions are carnivorous arachnids, recognizable 
for their grasping pincers and forward curving tail 
with a stinger on the end. They are found in many 
different habitats, but primarily in deserts and other 
harsh environments and climates. In order to hunt 
their typical prey—insects and small mammals and 
reptiles—scorpions entrap them in their claws, then 
finish them off by injecting venom through their 
stingers. Giant scorpions are much deadlier and more 
dangerous than typical scorpions, with venom that can 
easily kill the average person. They are generally found 
in subterranean or desert caverns during the day, then 
stalk their chosen habitats during the night to hunt

sea_horses.content:
These tiny fish are named for the equine shape of 
their heads. Found in shallow salt waters in tropical 
and temperate climates, sea horses are scattered 
throughout coral reefs. Their prehensile tails are 
used to anchor themselves to seaweed or coral, and 
combined with their ability to camouflage, they make 
masterful ambush predators—lying in wait to suck 
up small crustaceans. Giant sea horses make homes in 
deeper waters and can effectively defend themselves 
against large predators by ramming them with their

shadow.content:
These haunting undead beings are created when 
the shadow of a corpse is bound to its body by 
necromantic magics—where it overtakes and 
consumes the corpse to take its amorphous shape. 
Shadows are capable of slipping through mere 
cracks and can hide almost imperceptibly in areas of 
darkness. Combined with their resistance to many 
forms of damage and their ability to sap the strength 
of creatures they touch, they make uncanny assassins.
One known byproduct of shadows is that their 
draining touch leaves necromantic magics within 
a slain person, causing that being’s shadow to fuse 
with the body and propagate a new undead creature. 
This shadow is not bound to any necromancer or 
spellcaster, and thus wanders of their own accord, 
seeking victims reminiscent of the enemies they had 
in their former life. Shadows are notably vulnerable 
to divine magics, and so priests and holy warriors 
are often sought to purge them when a shadow is 
discovered to be preying upon a community.

shambling_mound.content:
Within dense swamps and jungles, towns warn 
unwary travelers of overgrown, wandering vegetation 
that swallows creatures whole. Known as shambling 
mounds, these hulking, sentient plants are made of 
entangled and writhing fronds, vines, and moss. In 
order to survive, they engulf organic matter and leech 
nutrients from them for days or weeks. This matter 
can be other plants, animals, or unwitting wanderers.
By lurking beneath water or within dense foliage, 
shambling mounds lie in wait until they hear 
movement nearby, whereupon they lurch out and 
engulf their prey. The plants that make up a shambling 
mound are coated in a unique substance that makes 
them highly resilient to heat and frost, and even 
can harness the energy of lightning to regenerate 
damaged parts.

sharks.content:

the waters for telltale fins, sharks are aquatic apex 
predators that inhabit the seas. Their carnivorous 
diets typically include fish, crustaceans, and marine 
mammals, but can extend to people. While usually 
found in oceanic habitats, there are some freshwater 
sharks. Keen and swift hunters, most sharks are 
solitary beasts, but certain types—such as the small 
reef shark, which inhabits shallower waters and coral 
reefs—gather in small packs to hunt. Giant sharks 
are found in deep oceans. Utterly fearless, they prey 
on anything that crosses their path, including whales 
and seafaring people. Some aquatic peoples, such as

shield_guardian.content:
A shield guardian is an advanced form of magical 
construct, created by a spellcaster for the explicit 
purpose of defending a person—typically themselves. 
Upon creation, a shield guardian is bound to an 
amulet, forged alongside the construct. The amulet 
denotes the guardian’s ward and can be used to 
telepathically dictate the construct’s actions as long 
as the amulet and guardian are on the same plane of 
existence. Otherwise, the shield guardian is stationary. 
In addition, while within a certain distance of the 
guardian, the amulet transfers damage endured by the 
wielder to the construct.
The core of a shield guardian has the capability to 
hold a spell—either to be used on command or under 
set conditions. Those who rely on shield guardians 
tend to either store another defensive measure or a 
devastating offensive surprise. Shield guardians are 
built durably and can magically repair themselves to 
better protect the bearer of their amulets. If a shield 
guardian’s amulet is damaged, the construct might 
begin to act erratically; if it is broken, the construct 
ceases to function until the amulet is repaired.

skeleton.content:
The telltale clattering of bones strikes fear into the 
hearts of adventurers, usually serving as a warning 
for whatever danger lurks ahead. Those bones might 
be moving of their own accord, rattling in malicious 
pursuit. Skeletons are the byproduct of necromantic 
magics raising corpses that are so old as to be reduced 
to mere bones. 
While skeletons can be raised intentionally, they are 
often the byproduct of dark magics gradually building 
up in an area of great death and tragedy, such as an 
ancient battlefield or a castle abandoned because of 
plague. The average skeleton retains only a vestigial 
sense of self, enough to recall weapon skills and innate 
magic but little else. Skeletons are faster than zombies 
due to being unburdened by injured flesh and muscle, 
but their exposed bones are brittle and vulnerable to 
well-placed brute force.
Skeleton Template
This template can be applied to any beast, giant, or 
person stat block, provided the base creature has 
bones. The creature keeps its statistics, except as 
follows.
Type. The skeleton’s type is undead.
Armor Scraps. The skeleton’s defense is 11 + its 
Agility, or 12 + its Agility if it is Large or larger.
Speed. The skeleton loses any flying or 
swimming speed.
Abilities. Replace the base creature’s abilities with 
the following: its Health is +2, its Wisdom is −1, and 
its Presence is −3. In addition, its Intelligence is −3 or 
the base creature’s Intelligence, whichever is lower.
Vulnerabilities and Immunities. The skeleton gains 
vulnerability to bludgeoning damage and immunity 
to poison damage and the exhaustion and sickened 
conditions.
Senses. The skeleton’s primary sense is sight, and it 
gains darkvision out to a range of 60 feet.
Mindless. The skeleton loses the memories and 
knowledge of its former life. It loses any spellcasting 
ability the base creature might have had, but it retains 
its Innate Spellcasting, if any.
Languages. The skeleton understands the languages 
it knew in life but can’t speak.

snakes.content:
The snake is a carnivorous reptile with a long, 
sinuous body lacking limbs. They are found in diverse 
habitats, ranging from forests and jungles to prairies 
and deserts, with some species even dwelling in and 
around water. While their exact diet is dependent on 
species, snakes are known to eat mammals, insects, 
amphibians, fish, and other reptiles. Giant snakes eat 
prey more appropriate to their size, including people. 
Snakes swallow their prey whole, even if it is much 
larger than they are, and different kinds of snakes 
subdue their meals differently.
Constrictor snakes coil their body around prey and 
suffocate them; they often grow to massive sizes even 
outside of magical regions. Venomous snakes use 
their fangs to inject venom, which grows more potent 
the bigger they are. It is not unheard of for swarms 
of venomous snakes to be used in traps or defenses. 
A flying snake is a brightly colored, winged serpent 
found in jungles. People sometimes domesticate 
flying snakes to serve as messengers that deliver scrolls 
wrapped in their coils.

Several cultures and communities have mastered the 
art of the spear to hunt and defend their people. Those 
warriors who learn the spear are skilled at wielding 
it not only up close—with one hand and two—but 
also from afar. While one of these warriors is effective 
alone, they know tactics that make them even more 
deadly as a team, which become useful against groups 
of foes or a single powerful enemy.

specter.content:
Specters are often mistaken for particularly violent 
ghosts, but while ghosts are souls with business left 
unfinished at the time of their passing, specters 
are souls ripped from their bodies by dark magic. 
Skilled necromancers purposefully create specters to 
bind them, for a specter can seep through the cracks 
in defenses to sap the life from sleeping creatures. 
However, the malevolent nature of a specter’s creation 
leaves them vulnerable to the blinding radiance of 
daylight, so they are most useful at night.
A specter left unbound or whose necromancer dies 
is left adrift. Much like ghosts, these specters haunt 
locations important to them and try to complete 
their unfinished business, though their methods are 
typically violent. Due to the nature of their creation, 
they are loath to trust living people, despite needing 
assistance to peacefully pass on. Some ways to aid a 
specter include a holy rite or painstaking patience to 
calm them and resolve their business.

sphinxes.content:
Enigmatic creatures with the body of a lion, the wings 
of an eagle, and the face of a person, sphinxes are 
thought to be the creations of gods of knowledge or 
magic. They are notably inscrutable, with minds that 
are labyrinthine and unknowable to mortals—even 
through use of magic—and are capable of sensing and 
misdirecting divination. 
Ferociously strong and keenly intelligent, sphinxes 
are divided into the smaller gnosisphinxes and 
the larger, and more powerful, sophisphinxes. A 
sophisphinx’s thrice-bellowed roar can plant terror and 
torpor in the strongest-willed creatures, even while 
rupturing eardrums. All sphinxes are known for their 
extensive knowledge of useful and restorative spells. 
It is rumored in old tales that one suffering from an 
affliction or curse can trade valuable knowledge to a 
sphinx in exchange for a cure.
Sphinxes are often charged with guarding 
repositories of ancient knowledge or powerful magical 
artifacts—either by the gods that created them 
or spellcasters they have made deals with. Often 
these charges are meant to protect the unworthy or 
foolish from gaining access, rather than keeping all 
individuals at bay. As such, sphinxes prefer to judge 
the worth of would-be heroes through tests of wit, 
knowledge, and wisdom over tests of combat.

spiders.content:
A spider is a predatory arachnid that uses a sticky 
substance to weave webs to entrap their prey. Normal-
sized spiders typically prey upon insects, fellow 
spiders, or sometimes larger beasts, such as small birds 
and lizards. Some spiders are slightly venomous, but 
giant spiders have a venom that is deadlier to people. 
Much how their smaller kin snare their prey, a giant 
spider spins elaborate webs or shoots sticky strands 
of webbing from their abdomen. Giant spiders are 
most commonly found underground, making their 
lairs on ceilings or in dark, web-filled crevices. Such 
lairs are often festooned with web cocoons holding 
past victims. Smaller than a giant spider, a giant wolf 
spider hunts across open ground or hides in a burrow, 
crevice, or hidden cavity beneath debris.
While specific conditions or magic can influence 
the growth of a giant spider, magical influence can 
also imbue spiders with unusual abilities, such as 
those seen in phase spiders. A phase spider possesses 
the magical ability to phase in and out of the Ethereal 
Plane. They seem to appear out of nowhere and 
quickly vanish after attacking. Their movement on the 
Ethereal Plane before coming back to a material plane 
makes them seem to teleport.

sprite.content:
Sprites resemble people, though barely a hand’s 
height tall, with beautiful, insect-shaped wings. These 
vivacious fey have enough courage for a soul ten times 
their size, and designate themselves as protectors of fey 
communities, whether they are asked to or not. Sprites 
set up their outposts at the edges of said communities, 
ever vigilant for trespassers. While their weapons are 
too small to deal significant damage to larger foes, the 
toxin they coat their arrows with can render even the 
most sizable creature unconscious. 
With their invisibility magic, sprites stalk creatures 
that approach fey lands, using a special power innate 
to sprites to glean whether the intentions of their 
heart are positive. If they are, sprites allow the guests 
to greet the fey community. If they are not, sprites 
handle intruders with cleverly placed traps, toxin-laced 
arrows, or other clever deceptions and distractions. 
Some sprites reject the call of defending other fey 
and instead use their magic elsewhere in the planes—
causing mischief for ne’er-do-wells or sabotaging 
villains.

stirge.content:
Stirges are infamous, blood-sucking pests, resembling 
a cross between an oversized moth and a mosquito. 
They are fragile creatures but can cause significant 
distress and injury, as they attach themselves to 
creatures and drain blood until sated. Stirges use their 
barbed mouth to pierce flesh and remain hooked 
to their victim while draining blood through a thin 
proboscis inserted into the wound. 
They are active primarily at night and make their 
nests in dark areas within populated areas. Some 
structures they often nest in are storehouses, barns, 
and abandoned buildings. Certain subspecies of 
stirges prefer the blood of other creatures over people 
and thus make their nests in ruins and caves where 
beasts and monsters lurk—though they are not 
above feasting from a passing adventurer when their 
preferred food is scarce.

swarm_of_insects.content:

where social insects gather together for any number 
of reasons, including changes in environment or 
ecosystem. While swarms of insects can be pests that 
cause damage to buildings or crops, they are typically 
not aggressive unless provoked. However, insects that 
swarm due to magic—whether from latent energies 
or being specifically summoned or controlled—are 
often more hostile than their natural counterparts. An 
aggressive swarm can be difficult to deal with, but over 
time, a swarm can be culled enough that it poses less 
of a danger until it can be fully handled or contained.

tarrasque.content:
Ancient tales of calamitous destruction speak of 
a colossal titan—a progenitor monster who lays 
waste to entire lands. Known only as the tarrasque, 
this reptilian behemoth instills more fear than the 
krakens lurking beneath the waves or the dragons that 
dominate the skies. Legends speak of impenetrable 
scales that repel even the most masterful spellcraft, 
as well as teeth and claws stronger and deadlier 
than most well-crafted adamantine. A sweep of the 
tarrasque’s tail can level a building and their horns can 
gouge the finest armor. 
It is said that the tarrasque has existed since the 
creation of the world. Some myths claim the titan is 
a pet of a powerful or perhaps forgotten god. Other 
scrawled legends name the creature as a scourge sent 
to devour the world in the throes of its creation. 
Still other writings would say the world itself beget 
the tarrasque—a primordial force of destruction to 
balance the cosmological creation that the world 
represents.
What is known as truth is that the tarrasque only 
emerges at pivotal moments—in those times of 
chaos and unrest that are the makings of true heroes 
and have the potential to carve stories that resonate 
throughout the ages. It is as if the tarrasque senses 
such coming calamities. Is there any truth to the 
whispers that say the tarrasque does not come to fulfill 
them, but instead to stop them?

tigers.content:
Tigers are known as one of the largest felines, and are 
distinguised from other by their distinctive orange 
pelts and dark stripes. They are solitary and territorial 
hunters, claiming land in habitats such as rain forests, 
grasslands, and savannas and hunting animals like deer 
and wild boar. 
Despite their name, saber-toothed tigers are not 
directly related to striped tigers. Saber-toothed tigers 
are smaller, with short, thick legs and a stocky body, 
along with the foot-long, curved canine teeth that 
give them their name. They are found in grasslands 
and open woodlands, hunting similar prey to regular 
tigers, as well as young mammoths and monsters. 
Both tigers are ambush predators, hiding or stalking 
their prey until they pounce.

tracyn.content:
The tracyn may look like a monster, but it can be 
tamed. Doing so is not for the faint of heart. The first 
trick is finding one. Because the creature is literally 
on fire at all times, and grows especially heated when 
active or angered, the tracyn lives far from anything 
flammable. Remote coastlines, hot deserts, and blasted 
wastelands are the most likely places.
Next, earning the tracyn’s trust is no small feat. 
With animal-like intelligence, the tracyn is naturally 
mistrustful. Coax it with meat and slow movements, 
along with the patience required for it to grow 
accustomed to your presence for several weeks. If it 
begins to follow you, you know you have a faithful 
companion for a lifetime.

treant.content:
In the hearts of ancient forests where nature’s magic 
thrives and flourishes, the oldest trees become treants. 
After being blessed by nature deities or venerable 
archfey, these chosen trees develop giant-like features 
and uproot themselves from the earth. The faces they 
grow, knotted and carved into their bark, allow them 
to speak the wisdom they have gathered over centuries 
or longer of listening to powerful beings and the 
vastness of the earth. 
Some treants are active caretakers of their forests, 
tending to creatures and other plants, while others 
protect the land from intruders who would wantonly 
pillage its resources. Though few and far between, 
some aged treants re-root themselves into the earth, 
nurturing groves through their roots and providing 
insight to those who make a pilgrimage to meet them. 
Treants are generally slow to anger, but those who 
disrespect their lands always earn a treant’s ire. To 
defend their land, treants rally the forest itself to rise 
up against those who mean it harm.

unicorn.content:
The mythical unicorn is a celestial creature that 
appears as a snow white horse with a single, spiraling 
horn protruding from its forehead. These divine 
creatures are the protectors of hallowed sites, such as 
sacred springs, blessed fountains, or secluded temples. 
Their holy strength is concentrated in their horn, 
which not only allows them to innately cast magic, 
but also pierces mundane defenses. A mere touch from 
a unicorn’s horn can hallow waters and purge them of 
impurities like poison, disease, or pollution.
Unicorns innately sense the intentions of any 
creature that is near them, and they respond 
accordingly. Those with good and righteous intentions 
are allowed to pass or, in certain cases, are only 
permitted after being tested in a trial of strength 
against the celestial guardian. However, those who 
harbor ill will or ideals contrary to the unicorn are 
either driven from the unicorn’s domain or trampled 
under its hooves. 
It is unwise to hunt unicorns, but their horns are 
a sought-after reagent in the creation of powerful 
wands, as well as for restorative potions and cures. 
If the need is dire and the cause just, a unicorn may 
shed its horn—sacrificing its power until the horn 
regrows—and allow it to be taken.

vampires.content:
There are several accounts of the origins of vampires. 
One is that the curse was inflicted upon decadent 
mortals by judgmental fiends, another is that they 
were first raised by a bloodthirsty death god, and yet 
others claim mortal necromancers created the unholy 
affliction themselves. What is known and true is that 
vampires are undead who retain their intelligence 
and identity, but have an appetite for blood that they 
must sate lest they wither to dust. The fanged bite of a 
vampire allows them to pierce the flesh of victims and 
drain their blood.
The curse of vampirism grants its victims incredible 
strength, as well as innate powers, such as the ability 
to transform into a bat and regenerate from near-
fatal injuries. However, the curse also confers unusual 
weaknesses, like an incredible vulnerability to sunlight 
and running water.
Many vampires prey on victims in the night, then 
hide during the day, stirring up chaos and confusion 
when bodies drained of blood turn up. Others use 
their might to gather power and wealth, lording over 
townsfolk who fear their influence, power, and hunger. 
Yet, not all vampires survive by wickedness. Some 
subsist on the less nourishing blood of animals to 
avoid causing harm and help others rather than reign 
over them. While many good-intentioned vampires 
hide what they are for fear of scorn, others embrace it 
and are embraced in turn.
A vampire’s bite carries the curse of vampirism, 
and a creature that succumbs to it rises as a vampire 
spawn. While driven by the same thirst for blood and 
limited by the same weaknesses as a regular vampire, 
a spawn does not have the same powers. The vampire 
that created the spawn can elevate them to true 
vampirehood, so spawn that seek power and don’t 
despise their state serve their vampire sire or madam 
in hopes of cultivating enough favor to ascend.

veteran.content:
Of those who comprise the ranks of adventurers, 
armies, and other such groups, there are people 
who have lasted longer than others. Tempered and 
strengthened by combat and experience, these veterans 
have learned from what they’ve endured. While many 
veterans are elders of their people, experience does not 
always equal years—for some young souls see far more 
combat than those twice their age. Some veterans stay 
where they are, while others become sellswords. Still 
others put away their weapons to choose a different 
path. No matter what, a veteran never forgets their 
skills, and it is best not to underestimate them.

The volcanopede is a massive insect that begins its life 
within magma chambers, maturing in about a century. 
These voracious monsters feed on a mixture of meat 
and minerals. Volcanopedes of all ages cause more 
frequent eruptions, as they burrow about, creating 
new magma flows. While the young cannot survive 
on the cold surface, mature volcanopedes can tolerate 
doing so for short periods and sometimes burrow 
into local settlements to feed, creating desolation in 
their wake.

vultures.content:
Vultures are scavenger birds that are easily recognized 
by their bald heads, which help keep them clean 
while they feast on carrion. They are primarily found 
in deserts, savannas, and grasslands. A vulture’s wide 
wingspan allows them to glide for hours, either while 
seeking food or waiting for a future meal to die. A 
giant vulture has advanced intelligence. Unlike its 
smaller kin, it attacks a wounded creature to hasten 
its end. Giant vultures have been known to pursue a 
thirsty, starving creature for days. Given that vultures 
devour carcasses and often gather in flocks around 
them, vultures are sometimes considered omens

If a volcaopede survives for a millennia or more, it grows into 
a supervolcanopede, a Gargantuan creature that most living 
beings flee from. The supervolcanopede is rarely content to live 
in its birth volcano, but travels to an area devoid of competitors. 
Upon finding a suitable location, they burrow deep enough to 
reach magma, thus creating a new and very active volcano. 
Creatures of fire and lava are drawn to the lair like moths. A 
supervolcanopede is so intelligent and awe-inspiring that some 
become objects of worship.

weasels.content:
The small, sleek weasel is a carnivorous mammal that 
is a far more dangerous predator than it appears. 
Their long body allows weasels to follow prey into 
their burrows. As cunning hunters, they can kill 
prey that is much bigger than them, such as squirrels 
and rabbits. Weasels thrive in fields, woodlands, and 
thickets, as well as near farmlands, where they are 
often considered vermin for their tendency to steal 
chicken and eggs. While typically not aggressive 
toward people, they attack if frightened. Giant weasels 
are uncommon, but they have a far more voracious 
appetite than their smaller kind, and as such, are a 
much greater nuisance to communities with larger 
livestock and other tempting resources.

werefolk.content:
There is no widely accepted origin of werefolk. Some 
claim it was a curse, the vengeance of a wild god upon 
people who defiled nature. Others believe it either 
fiendish in source—the aftermath of a devil deal gone 
wrong—or bestowed by the whims of a bored fey. 
Then there are those who argue it was a mortal-made 
affair, the profane experiments of mages drawing on 
bestial strength.
People fear contracting lycanthropy and similar 
curses, and no matter their beginnings, they are now 
transmitted through the bite of werefolk or passed 
down through their lineage. There are several types 
of werefolk, each bearing the aspect of a different 
beast. The curse allows a transformation from person 
to beast, or to a ferocious, hybrid creature. Some

wight.content:
The uncanny appearance of a wight might trick one 
into believing they are a living person, but the ashen 
pallor of their skin, the subtle glow to their eyes, and 
their lack of breath gives them away. Wights are raised 
from willing people, those who choose to shed the 
mortality of their weak bodies for an immortal and 
undead form. In contrast to lesser undead, wights 
retain their sense of self and gain greater power, such 
as unnatural resilience and the ability to drain life 
from other creatures. However, this newfound might 
comes at a cost: wights are drastically weakened while 
in direct sunlight.
As such, wights act in darkness when their true 
nature is better concealed and they are at full strength. 
Many owe allegiance to the spellcaster who granted 
them their form and often coordinate other undead or 
handle delicate missions on the necromancer’s behalf. 
Others strike out on their own, either by betraying 
the spellcaster or offering something of value to pay

willowisp.content:
Travelers are often warned to beware glowing lights 
at the edge of their vision, lest they be led astray by 
will-o’-wisps. In areas steeped in magic, wayfarers who 
get lost before meeting a tragic end may rise as orbs of 
ghostly light known as will-o’-wisps. These souls are 
bound to the region where they died, able to do little 
more than speak in haunting echoes and control their 
own light.
Many will-o’-wisps, bitter over their fate, 
maliciously appear before travelers, pretending to be 
the warm light of safety in the distance to lead another 
wandering soul to their demise and consume their life. 
Other will-o’-wisps, holding onto their compassion, 
refuse to let another fall to their same fate—these 
wisps lead lost travelers away from danger and toward 
a nearby camp or community. In rare cases, a powerful 
fey may curse an individual who has wronged them, 
transforming them into a will-o’-wisp and binding 
them to protect a sacred fey treasure or area from 
those who would seek to steal or harm it.

wolves.content:
Wolves are widespread canines and predators. Found 
in habitats—including forests, grasslands, deserts, 
tundras, and mountains—throughout the Material 
Planes, they hunt deer, sheep, and bison, along with 
smaller mammals when large prey is scarce. They 
gather in packs, allowing them to hunt much larger 
animals than they could alone. Known for their loyalty 
and ferocity, it is not uncommon to find wolves as the 
companions of rangers and other adventurers. Dire 
wolves are much larger wolves, hardier and stronger 
than their regular-sized kin. They can survive in much 
harsher environments, and packs of dire wolves prey 
on beasts and monsters like mammoths and chimeras.
The arctic-dwelling winter wolf is as large as a 
dire wolf but has snow-white fur and pale blue eyes. 
Frost giants use these creatures as guards and hunting 
companions, putting the wolves’ deadly breath 
weapon to use against their foes. Winter wolves 
communicate with one another telepathically, but 
they understand Giant well enough to follow simple 
conversations.
